summary: Behind-the-scenes reconstruction of Brandon Mercer's flight from Williamsburg to the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel, his ripped-up ticket on East Jefferson Avenue, his refusal of entry into Canada at 555 Goyeau Street / 35 Park Street East, and his arrest by Deputy U.S. Marshals on Cass Avenue.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 5, Chapter 1, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road/north-henry-street-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-file/part-2-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-blind-leap-at-boundary-street-crown-burger-open-radio-on-route-20-dad-at-indian-river-road) and [***Part 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road/north-henry-street-six-buses-from-williamsburg-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-file/part-3-the-goyeau-street-tunnel-bus-the-trashed-ticket-on-east-jefferson-avenue-protected-non-traveling-complainant), readers watch nineteen-year-old twins **Katie and Nathaniel Prairie** take a blind leap of faith onto the `4:00 PM` **CTTA Grey Line** bus outside the **Williamsburg Transportation Center** on Saturday, October 16, 2004—riding six buses across two transit agencies to meet their father **David Prairie** at **Military Highway and Indian River Road** at `8:01 PM`—and then accompany David to the **Walter E. Hoffman United States Courthouse** on Granby Street in Norfolk four days later. This Backstage dossier reconstructs what happened in between from the perspective of the **Williamsburg Police Department**, the **Canada Border Services Agency (`CBSA`)**, **U.S. Customs and Border Protection (`CBP`)**, and the **United States Marshals Service**.

---

## 1. Saturday Afternoon & Night, October 16, 2004 (`3:52 PM – 11:30 PM`): The Blind Ticket Counter at `468 North Boundary Street`

When twenty-two-year-old **Brandon Mercer** ordered nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate to wait outside on the brick bus loop of the **Williamsburg Transportation Center** while he stepped inside the historic red-brick depot, he walked up to an interior **American Rail Transit System (`ARTS`)** ticket counter with **zero window line of sight** to the bus bays outside.

1. **Two Full-Price, Non-Refundable Regular Adult Tickets to Detroit (`DET`):**
   Because Brandon had never ridden public transit with disabled riders, he had no idea ARTS offered discounted *Passenger with a Disability (`PWD`) + Companion* tariffs. Instead, he emptied nearly his entire checking account (`leaving $4.12 on his station ATM receipt`) to pay cash for **two full-price, non-refundable Regular Adult one-way rail-and-thruway tickets to Detroit, Michigan**—intending to haul Katie across the river into Ontario for a "fresh start" and abandon Nate stranded on the Williamsburg platform once the train pulled in.
2. **Why Brandon Booked Detroit + Tunnel Bus Instead of Cross-Border Rail:**
   Hidden inside a lockbox at the house off **North Henry Street** were **two external hard drives** containing skimmed resort front-desk credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity profiles. Afraid that booking a direct cross-border ARTS train into Ontario would transmit his name on an advance electronic passenger manifest hours before reaching the border, Brandon convinced himself that riding domestically to Detroit and walking onto a municipal **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus** would let him slip quietly into Canada and sign up for free **Ontario Health Insurance Plan (`OHIP`)** coverage.
3. **Walking Out to an Empty Brick Loop (`4:02 PM`):**
   When the manual multi-segment paper ticket jacket finished printing and Brandon pushed back out the double doors, both `SwiftChair` powerchairs were gone—already rolling south down Jamestown Road aboard the `4:00 PM` **CTTA Grey Line** toward Lee Hall. Realizing Katie and Nate were heading straight to **David Prairie** and the police—and furious at the thought of eating two expensive, non-refundable Regular Adult tickets—Brandon hurried two blocks back to North Henry Street, stuffed his clothes and both contraband hard drives into a fifty-pound canvas duffel bag, and boarded the evening northbound **ARTS** train toward Washington, Toledo, and Detroit using his own valid Regular Adult ticket.

---

## 2. Sunday Afternoon, October 17, 2004 (`3:45 PM – 4:50 PM`): East Jefferson Avenue, The Tunnel Bus Farebox, & `555 Goyeau Street` / `35 Park Street East`

Stepping off his connecting thruway coach in downtown **Detroit, Michigan** on Sunday afternoon after twenty hours without sleep, Brandon walked down toward the **Detroit-Windsor Tunnel** plaza at **East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street**—and made three consecutive blunders before he even reached a Canadian border podium:

* **Ripping Up Katie's Unused Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue (`3:50 PM`):**
  Furious every time he looked at Katie's unused Regular Adult voucher inside the yellow ARTS ticket jacket, Brandon tore Katie's ticket and the attached purchase receipt in half and threw both into a municipal trash barrel on **East Jefferson Avenue**—unknowingly destroying the unused ticket's residual exchange value that could have paid his bus fare back to Virginia.
* **The Transit Windsor Farebox Surprise (`4:00 PM`):**
  Boarding the cross-border **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus**, Brandon discovered that Transit Windsor accepted U.S. currency strictly at a **`1:1` par rate** rather than giving an exchange premium, that the Canadian electronic coin validator rejected **American dimes** and **American gold-colored one-dollar coins** (`because Canadian dimes use different metallic composition and Loonies have a distinct eleven-sided signature`), and that municipal fareboxes issue **zero change**. Forced to shove his very last **ten-dollar U.S. bill** into the exact-fare slot to pay a single tunnel fare, Brandon rode under the Detroit River into Ontario with exactly **`$1.75` in American quarters** left in his pocket.
* **Refusal of Entry at `555 Goyeau Street` & `35 Park Street East` (`4:15 PM – 4:50 PM`):**
  Emerging onto the Canadian inspection plaza at **`555 Goyeau Street`** (near **Wyandotte Street East**), all Tunnel Bus passengers were directed inside the **CBSA Windsor Tunnel District Operations building** at **`35 Park Street East`**. Referred to Secondary Inspection by **CBSA Officer Vance** after snapping that as an American citizen with a birth certificate he had a "right" to enter Canada, Brandon had his duffel bag unpacked on the steel inspection table—revealing his birth certificate folder, `$1.75` in pocket quarters, his `$4.12` Williamsburg ATM slip, two external hard drives, and three pages of printed internet notes about moving permanently to Ontario and signing up for **`OHIP`**. Informed that American tourists have zero legal right to reside in Canada or receive provincial healthcare, Brandon was formally refused entry under **Sections 20 and 39 of Canada's *Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (`IRPA`)*** and—after lunging at the counter in an outburst—driven back through the tunnel in the caged rear compartment of a marked **CBSA** enforcement van.

---

## 3. Sunday Evening to Tuesday (`October 17–19, 2004`): The CBP Contraband Seizure on Randolph Street & The U.S. Marshals Arrest on Cass Avenue

At `5:05 PM` on Sunday evening, CBSA officers escorted Brandon straight through the security door of the **U.S. Customs and Border Protection (`CBP`)** compound at **East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street** in Detroit:

1. **Mandatory Warrantless Border Search (`19 U.S.C. § 1582`):**
   Conducting a routine border examination of a foreign-refused traveler, Detroit CBP officers powered on the **two external hard drives** in Brandon's duffel bag—uncovering hundreds of skimmed credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity files from Williamsburg hospitality registers, instantly elevating Brandon's local misconduct into a multi-count federal wire-fraud and identity-theft prosecution.
2. **Arrested Outside the Men's Shelter on Cass Avenue (`Tuesday, October 19, 2004`):**
   Released onto **East Jefferson Avenue** with `$1.75` in his pocket while CBP forensic agents transmitted the seized drive images to federal prosecutors in Virginia and Michigan, Brandon walked nine blocks northwest to a brick men's homeless shelter on **Cass Avenue**—where **Deputy United States Marshals** arrested him on federal felony warrants without incident.
3. **`Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction)` (`Wednesday, October 20, 2004`):**
   Because the Williamsburg station security camera and ARTS ticket audit proved Katie never boarded the train and escaped six hundred miles away while Brandon destroyed her unused ticket himself on East Jefferson Avenue, **Special Agent Morales** at the **Walter E. Hoffman U.S. Courthouse on Granby Street** confirmed that Katie's name carried a permanent **`Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction)`** shield—certifying zero criminal, civil, or immigration infractions in both U.S. and Canadian databases for life.

When twenty-two-year-old Brandon Mercer ordered nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate to wait outside on the brick bus loop of the Williamsburg Transportation Center while he stepped inside the historic red-brick depot, he walked up to an interior American Rail Transit System (ARTS) ticket counter with zero window line of sight to the bus bays outside.

  1. Two Full-Price, Non-Refundable Regular Adult Tickets to Detroit (DET):
    Because Brandon had never ridden public transit with disabled riders, he had no idea ARTS offered discounted Passenger with a Disability (PWD) + Companion tariffs. Instead, he emptied nearly his entire checking account (leaving $4.12 on his station ATM receipt) to pay cash for two full-price, non-refundable Regular Adult one-way rail-and-thruway tickets to Detroit, Michigan—intending to haul Katie across the river into Ontario for a "fresh start" and abandon Nate stranded on the Williamsburg platform once the train pulled in.
  2. Why Brandon Booked Detroit + Tunnel Bus Instead of Cross-Border Rail:
    Hidden inside a lockbox at the house off North Henry Street were two external hard drives containing skimmed resort front-desk credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity profiles. Afraid that booking a direct cross-border ARTS train into Ontario would transmit his name on an advance electronic passenger manifest hours before reaching the border, Brandon convinced himself that riding domestically to Detroit and walking onto a municipal Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus would let him slip quietly into Canada and sign up for free Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) coverage.
  3. Walking Out to an Empty Brick Loop (4:02 PM):
    When the manual multi-segment paper ticket jacket finished printing and Brandon pushed back out the double doors, both SwiftChair powerchairs were gone—already rolling south down Jamestown Road aboard the 4:00 PM CTTA Grey Line toward Lee Hall. Realizing Katie and Nate were heading straight to David Prairie and the police—and furious at the thought of eating two expensive, non-refundable Regular Adult tickets—Brandon hurried two blocks back to North Henry Street, stuffed his clothes and both contraband hard drives into a fifty-pound canvas duffel bag, and boarded the evening northbound ARTS train toward Washington, Toledo, and Detroit using his own valid Regular Adult ticket.

2. Sunday Afternoon, October 17, 2004 (3:45 PM – 4:50 PM): East Jefferson Avenue, The Tunnel Bus Farebox, & 555 Goyeau Street / 35 Park Street East

Stepping off his connecting thruway coach in downtown Detroit, Michigan on Sunday afternoon after twenty hours without sleep, Brandon walked down toward the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel plaza at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street—and made three consecutive blunders before he even reached a Canadian border podium:

  • Ripping Up Katie's Unused Ticket on East Jefferson Avenue (3:50 PM):
    Furious every time he looked at Katie's unused Regular Adult voucher inside the yellow ARTS ticket jacket, Brandon tore Katie's ticket and the attached purchase receipt in half and threw both into a municipal trash barrel on East Jefferson Avenue—unknowingly destroying the unused ticket's residual exchange value that could have paid his bus fare back to Virginia.
  • The Transit Windsor Farebox Surprise (4:00 PM):
    Boarding the cross-border Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus, Brandon discovered that Transit Windsor accepted U.S. currency strictly at a 1:1 par rate rather than giving an exchange premium, that the Canadian electronic coin validator rejected American dimes and American gold-colored one-dollar coins (because Canadian dimes use different metallic composition and Loonies have a distinct eleven-sided signature), and that municipal fareboxes issue zero change. Forced to shove his very last ten-dollar U.S. bill into the exact-fare slot to pay a single tunnel fare, Brandon rode under the Detroit River into Ontario with exactly $1.75 in American quarters left in his pocket.
  • Refusal of Entry at 555 Goyeau Street & 35 Park Street East (4:15 PM – 4:50 PM):
    Emerging onto the Canadian inspection plaza at 555 Goyeau Street (near Wyandotte Street East), all Tunnel Bus passengers were directed inside the CBSA Windsor Tunnel District Operations building at 35 Park Street East. Referred to Secondary Inspection by CBSA Officer Vance after snapping that as an American citizen with a birth certificate he had a "right" to enter Canada, Brandon had his duffel bag unpacked on the steel inspection table—revealing his birth certificate folder, $1.75 in pocket quarters, his $4.12 Williamsburg ATM slip, two external hard drives, and three pages of printed internet notes about moving permanently to Ontario and signing up for OHIP. Informed that American tourists have zero legal right to reside in Canada or receive provincial healthcare, Brandon was formally refused entry under *Sections 20 and 39 of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and—after lunging at the counter in an outburst—driven back through the tunnel in the caged rear compartment of a marked CBSA* enforcement van.

3. Sunday Evening to Tuesday (October 17–19, 2004): The CBP Contraband Seizure on Randolph Street & The U.S. Marshals Arrest on Cass Avenue

At 5:05 PM on Sunday evening, CBSA officers escorted Brandon straight through the security door of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) compound at East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street in Detroit:

  1. Mandatory Warrantless Border Search (19 U.S.C. § 1582):
    Conducting a routine border examination of a foreign-refused traveler, Detroit CBP officers powered on the two external hard drives in Brandon's duffel bag—uncovering hundreds of skimmed credit-card magnetic-stripe dumps and stolen guest identity files from Williamsburg hospitality registers, instantly elevating Brandon's local misconduct into a multi-count federal wire-fraud and identity-theft prosecution.
  2. Arrested Outside the Men's Shelter on Cass Avenue (Tuesday, October 19, 2004):
    Released onto East Jefferson Avenue with $1.75 in his pocket while CBP forensic agents transmitted the seized drive images to federal prosecutors in Virginia and Michigan, Brandon walked nine blocks northwest to a brick men's homeless shelter on Cass Avenue—where Deputy United States Marshals arrested him on federal felony warrants without incident.
  3. Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) (Wednesday, October 20, 2004):
    Because the Williamsburg station security camera and ARTS ticket audit proved Katie never boarded the train and escaped six hundred miles away while Brandon destroyed her unused ticket himself on East Jefferson Avenue, Special Agent Morales at the Walter E. Hoffman U.S. Courthouse on Granby Street confirmed that Katie's name carried a permanent Protected Non-Traveling Complainant (V-W, Zero Infraction) shield—certifying zero criminal, civil, or immigration infractions in both U.S. and Canadian databases for life.

title: Dirty Old Tonomy Hill & Why Brandon's Tunnel-Bus Scheme Was Doomed Before He Left Williamsburg
subtitle: Why Cousin Chelsea Held All the Legal Cards in Newport—and the Two Transit Rules Brandon Mercer Never Bothered to Read
location: Tonomy Hill, Newport, Rhode Island & Williamsburg Transportation Center, Williamsburg, Virginia

> **Archival Note:** Across [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 5***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road), nineteen-year-old fraternal twins **Katie and Nathaniel Prairie** never spend a single night separated—surviving **Brandon Mercer** in Williamsburg (`Summer–October 2004`) and **Tiffany Sloan** in West Ocean View (`November 2004–November 2005`) side by side. This Backstage dossier examines two behind-the-scenes legal and transit realities from late 2004: the landlord-tenant power **Cousin Chelsea** unknowingly held inside her apartment on **Dirty Old Tonomy Hill** during [***Chapter 2, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/six-buses-from-williamsburg-sea-breeze-west-coming-home-to-arvin-road/tiffany-s-sea-breeze-west-apartment-dirty-old-tonomy-hill-coming-home-to-arvin-road/part-2-the-worst-christmas-ever-eighteen-stops-to-dirty-old-tonomy-hill-four-days-with-cousin-chelsea-the-west-main-road-shortcut-home), and the two transit rules that doomed Brandon Mercer before he ever walked out of the **Williamsburg Transportation Center**.

---

## 1. The Legal Irony on "Dirty Old Tonomy Hill" (`December 24–27, 2004`)

When nineteen-year-old **Katie and Nate** rode eighteen bus stops up the Eastern Seaboard to **Newport, Rhode Island** so their twenty-two-year-old paternal cousin **Chelsea** wouldn't spend her first Christmas Eve alone after losing her mother **Aunt Elizabeth** and **Grandma Ruth**, **Tiffany Sloan** flatly refused to stay behind in Norfolk and tagged along—spending Christmas Eve screaming at Katie, Nate, and Chelsea inside Chelsea's own living room.

Underneath Tiffany's bullying sat a remarkable legal irony that Chelsea's severe developmental disability prevented her from realizing:

1. **Chelsea Was the Sole Named Tenant on the Newport Housing Authority Lease:**
   The ground-floor unit in the World War II-era Tonomy Hill public-housing complex was **100% Cousin Chelsea's apartment**, leased solely in Chelsea's name through her Rhode Island adult developmental-disability caseworker. Tiffany had zero legal standing on the lease and hadn't paid a dime toward rent or utilities.
2. **One Phone Call Would Have Put Tiffany on the Curb in the December Wind:**
   Under Rhode Island landlord-tenant law and Newport Housing Authority guest rules, Tiffany was purely a revocable houseguest. At any moment between Friday afternoon and Monday morning, Chelsea had the complete legal authority to pick up her wall phone, call her caseworker or the **Newport Police Department**, and say she wanted Tiffany removed. Within twenty minutes, Newport officers would have escorted Tiffany Sloan out onto the curb in the Rhode Island cold while Katie and Nate stayed warm inside with their cousin.
3. **How Chelsea Enforced Her Own Version of an Eviction Anyway:**
   Because Chelsea's developmental delays meant she did not grasp statutory lease rights—viewing loud, angry adults as scary authority figures—she never knew she could call the police to remove Tiffany. Instead, Chelsea improvised the fiercest eviction she knew how: pulling **both Katie's wheelchair and Nate's wheelchair** down the hallway into her bedroom, slamming the door straight in Tiffany's face (*"Just Nate an' Katie! Mean Tiffany stay out!"*), twisting the brass thumb-lock shut for three straight nights, and guiding Katie and Nate out to **`OSTA Route 60`** on **West Main Road** Monday morning so they wouldn't miss their five-minute Pathfinder connection in Fall River.

---

## 2. Two Transit Rules Brandon Mercer Never Bothered to Read (`October 16–17, 2004`)

Two months earlier in Williamsburg, Brandon Mercer prided himself on outsmarting everyone around him—yet his entire October 16 plan collapsed because a car-driving abuser knew nothing about how rail tariffs or municipal cross-border transit actually work:

1. **Regular Adult Cash Fares vs. `PWD + Companion` Tariffs:**
   Walking up to the blind interior **ARTS** counter at `468 North Boundary Street` while Katie and Nate waited outside, Brandon asked for two Regular Adult one-way tickets to Detroit (`DET`) without ever realizing rail carriers offer discounted *Passenger with a Disability (`PWD`) + Companion* fares—and without realizing Regular Adult promotional cash fares carry strict forfeiture rules unless exchanged intact at a staffed counter. When he spitefully tore Katie's unused ticket and purchase receipt in half on **East Jefferson Avenue** in Detroit before boarding the **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus**, he threw away the only exchange credit that could have gotten him out of Michigan.
2. **Why Taking a City Bus Across an International Border Is *Harder*, Not Easier, Than Cross-Border Rail:**
   Afraid that boarding a direct New York-to-Toronto **ARTS** train would put his name on an advance electronic **CBSA** manifest while carrying two external hard drives full of skimmed credit-card numbers, Brandon assumed a local **Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus** worked like an ordinary city bus hop. In reality, walking into **`555 Goyeau Street`** and **`35 Park Street East`** off the Tunnel Bus with a fifty-pound duffel bag, zero return ticket, `$1.75` left after feeding his last `$10` U.S. bill into a no-change Canadian farebox that rejected American dimes and dollar coins, and printed notes about free **`OHIP`** provincial healthcare triggered an immediate **CBSA Secondary Inspection**—and guaranteed a mandatory warrantless **U.S. CBP** forensic search (`19 U.S.C. § 1582`) of both contraband hard drives the moment the caged CBSA van brought him back to **East Jefferson Avenue and Randolph Street**.

title: Inside Dirksen Room 511: Commissioner Sterling & Director Cross's Panic
subtitle: Nine Stages of Bureaucratic Collapse, the 2007 Magic-Marker Redaction Boomerang, & The Parked-Car Riot Act From Richmond
location: Room 511, Dirksen Senate Office Building & Constitution Avenue NE, Washington, D.C.
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 11, Chapter 3, Part 5)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 11, Chapter 3, Part 5: 34 C.F.R. § 361.38 & Strings Attached
summary: What was going through DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling's and RRC Director Evelyn Cross's minds inside Dirksen Room 511—and what happened in the hallway and on their three-way conference call with the Governor's Chief of Staff after they stumbled out.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 11, Chapter 3, Part 5***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-senator-from-virginia/first-train-from-norfolk-swearing-in-on-the-constitution-strings-attached-for-rrc/part-5-34-c-f-r-section-361-38-two-twelve-day-dropouts-in-room-511-strings-attached-at-the-subcommittee-hearing), the confrontation in **Room 511 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building** on Tuesday, February 16, 2027 is told strictly from **Nathaniel Prairie's** first-person POV beside **U.S. Senator Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia`)**. This Backstage dossier reveals what was going through the minds of **DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling** and **RRC Director Evelyn Cross** on the other side of the mahogany desk—and what happened in the forty minutes after they stumbled out into the fifth-floor hallway.

---

## 1. The Nine Stages of Bureaucratic Collapse Inside Dirksen Room 511

1. **Stage 1 — Smug Bureaucratic Overconfidence Walking Down the Hallway:**
   Walking into Dirksen Room 511 with their glossy spiral-bound `$18.5 million` Congressionally Directed Spending presentation, Sterling and Cross assumed this would be a ten-minute ceremonial photo-op: *"Senator Prairie is a forty-one-year-old wheelchair user from Virginia Beach. What disabled Senator on earth wouldn't rubber-stamp $18.5 million for Virginia's flagship rehabilitation center?"* Having checked the *Congressional Directory*—which listed only **Northwood High School (`VBCPS`)** and the **Community College of Hampton Roads (`CCHR`)**—neither executive had the slightest inkling that Katie or Nate had ever set foot in Fishersville.
2. **Stage 2 — Condescending Dismissal at Question #1 (*"Some Activist Sent Her an Email"*):**
   When Senator Prairie first asked about a twenty-one-year-old twin brother and sister in wheelchairs having their push-handles grabbed at **Barton Hall** in March 2007, Director Cross internally rolled her eyes—assuming a disgruntled former client had sent an email to the Senator's constituent inbox—and tried to brush it off with a canned line about modern staff training.
3. **Stage 3 — Baffled Unease at Questions #2 & #3 (*"Why Is a U.S. Senator Being So Forensically Hyperspecific About 2007?"*):**
   When Katie refused to let them pivot and drilled into hyper-granular 2007 operational details—two `CCHR` computer-science graduates forced to tour the **auto mechanics, woodworking, and nursing shops**, a Vocational Evaluator pitching a **Waynesboro ValueMart door-greeter partnership**, **VITA's seven-year-old `Quantum OS 2000 Professional`** locking down local web servers in the Bates-Harding lab, and staying stuck on **`Level 2` in Barton Hall** with **signed yellow paper Passes** because moving to **Cantor Hall** required earning **`Level 3`**—alarm bells started ringing inside both executives' heads:
   > *"Wait... why does a United States Senator know the exact color of the 2007 Level 2 paper passes in Barton Hall and VITA's desktop permissions in the Bates-Harding computer lab?! No K Street lobbyist or constituent form letter would ever know that!"*
4. **Stage 4 — Cold Creeping Dread at Question #4 (*"How Could Anyone Know About `MedStrip` Wound-Closure Strips and Lumpy Bags of Curtains Inside a Rec Hall Closet at 10:45 PM?!"*):**
   When Katie recounted the ninth afternoon (`Tuesday, March 13, 2007`)—the broken nose and split nasal bridge in the therapeutic pool, the twin brother covering his sister's bare chest while she held her bleeding nostrils with both hands until a towel arrived, the Bates-Harding clinic nurses pulling the split bridge skin together with **sterile `MedStrip` wound-closure strips** under a **seven-day white gauze bandage**, slipping down the darkened Rec Hall corridor at `10:45 PM` in street clothes, locking themselves inside a **seasonal storage closet** using **lumpy bags of curtains as pillows**, the night supervisor unlocking the door with a master key at `11:25 PM` and accusing them of having sex, and the twins daring him to walk to the Rec Hall desk phone and call their father in Alexandria right then and there—Sterling and Cross were internally panicking:
   > *"Even if someone in Richmond leaked an old 2007 disciplinary log, how does she know the exact sterile MedStrip wound-closure strips the nurses taped across that girl's nose—and no state form in DARS history ever recorded what the pillows inside a Rec Hall storage closet felt like at 10:45 PM! How on earth could she know that?!"*
   Still blind to the fact that the two forty-one-year-old `SwiftChair` users across the desk *were* those twins, they wondered out loud why she was being so oddly hyperspecific and threw up the **`34 C.F.R. § 361.38`** privacy wall—walking straight into Katie and Nate's trap.
5. **Stage 5 — The Split-Second Math Click & Stomach-Drop Vertigo (*"41 Minus 20 Is 21... OH GOD, IT'S THEM."*):**
   The instant Katie laced her fingers through Nate's across their `SwiftChair` armrests and said *"Because the twenty-one-year-old twin brother and sister in those March 2007 Barton Hall files are sitting right across this desk from you,"* every piece of the puzzle slammed together inside Sterling's and Cross's skulls at once:
   * `2027 - 2007 = 20 years ago`
   * `41 years old - 20 = 21 years old`
   * Fraternal twin brother and sister, both full-time wheelchair users, both graduated from `CCHR` in December 2006—three months before March 2007!
   * And the only reason `RRC` wasn't listed in the *Congressional Directory* was because **nobody puts a place they dropped out of after twelve days on their biography!**
   Both executives felt the floor drop out from under their stomachs as they realized they had just looked a sitting United States Senator in the eye, told her that her own broken nose and `MedStrip` bandage had never happened, and lectured her that **`34 C.F.R. § 361.38`** prohibited her from discussing her own life without her own permission.
6. **Stage 6 — The `"ValueMart Door Greeter"` & `Status 28 Dropout` Institutional Mortification:**
   Looking at the gold Senate lapel pin on Katie's blazer, Director Cross was hit by a wave of sheer professional horror: in March 2007, an RRC Vocational Evaluator had looked at **Katie Prairie**—a woman who already held an accredited college degree in computer science, who was about to build a multi-decade production software firm with her brother, and who would be elected to the Virginia Beach City Council, the House of Delegates, the Senate of Virginia, and the **United States Senate**—and told her to sit by the sliding doors of the **Waynesboro ValueMart as a door greeter**. Worse still, in DARS's own mainframes in Richmond right that second, **the United States Senator holding the purse strings over DARS's `$18.5 million` earmark was officially coded as a `Status 28` (*"Unsuccessful Rehabilitation — Client Dropped Out"*) failure!**
7. **Stage 7 — How DARS's Own 2007 Black-Marker Redaction Blindfolded Them in 2027:**
   Commissioner Sterling's mind raced wondering why his legislative liaison in Richmond hadn't flagged `"Prairie, Katie"` and `"Prairie, Nathaniel"` before letting him walk into Dirksen Room 511—only to realize the supreme poetic justice: back in April 2007, when DARS General Counsel blacked out Katie and Nate's names on the Tuesday pool log with a thick black magic marker as `[REDACTED UNDER 34 C.F.R. § 361.38 — STATUS 28 DROPOUT]` so **Evelyn Brooks's** lawyer couldn't locate them as witnesses, **DARS had also guaranteed that its own 2027 leadership wouldn't recognize the two redacted `Status 28` dropouts on that page until they were sitting across Senator Prairie's mahogany desk!**
8. **Stage 8 — The Second Nuclear Bomb (*Eyewitnesses to the 48 Hours Before Natalie Brooks Was Raped*):**
   When Nate quietly added *"And wait until you hear why our Thursday morning Level 1 restriction meeting with our counselor never happened on March 15, 2007,"* and Katie laid **Evelyn Brooks's notarized Guardianship/Conservatorship waiver and March 16, 2007 hospital ER/SANE report** on top of their funding binder, Sterling and Cross realized the Senator sitting on the Appropriations Subcommittee was a **firsthand eyewitness** proving that the exact male client who had broken her nose in the pool on Tuesday (`March 13`) had been left on campus by RRC, had used a scrambled keycard to rape **Natalie Brooks** on Wednesday night (`March 14`), and had been whisked onto a bus in Staunton at `7:50 AM` on Thursday (`March 15`) while housekeeping bleached the sheets.

---

## 2. Stage 9 — The Frantic Hallway Calls to Richmond & The Governor's Chief of Staff Reading Them the Riot Act (`3:10 PM – 4:15 PM`)

Stumbling out of Dirksen Room 511 with shaking hands—and forgetting their glossy spiral-bound `$18.5 million` funding binder on Katie's desk—Sterling and Cross started speed-dialing Richmond and Fishersville before they even reached the fifth-floor elevators:

* Within forty minutes, the basement archives in Richmond and Fishersville pulled the unredacted March 2007 (`03/04/2007 – 03/16/2007`) paper files for `Prairie, Katie` and `Prairie, Nathaniel` alongside the unredacted Tuesday pool log and Thursday infirmary/van dispatch records, confirming that **every single word Senator Prairie and Nate had said was 100% true**.
* Terrified of being annihilated on live television cameras in front of Natalie and her mother in **Dirksen Room 124** on Wednesday morning, both Sterling and Cross begged the **Virginia Secretary of Health and Human Resources** and **Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence** for permission to withdraw from Wednesday's Subcommittee witness panel and drive straight back to Richmond.
* Instead, **Arthur Lawrence**—who knew Katie Prairie well from her twelve years in the General Assembly and knew she answered her direct office phone herself—called Dirksen Room 511 on a **three-way conference call** with Sterling and Cross on the line from their parked car on Constitution Avenue.
* When Katie warned Lawrence on the speakerphone that *"if the Director and the Commissioner do not show up for the Subcommittee hearing on Wednesday morning, they will be facing compulsory subpoenas from the United States Senate"*—knowing she didn't need to claim unilateral subpoena power when the Subcommittee Chairman was ready to back her—Lawrence heard the unspoken final sentence loud and clear (*"Arthur, get them into those chairs voluntarily, because neither you nor the Governor wants to find out what happens next"*) and ordered Sterling and Cross into Dirksen Room 124 at nine o'clock sharp so they wouldn't jeopardize Virginia's entire **`$92+ million` share of federal Title I Rehabilitation Act matching funds**.

title: The $14 Million DSCC Primary Shock, Opposing Leader Schuman, The 211–204 Lame-Duck False Dawn, & The Senate Wheelchair Caucus
subtitle: Inside Retiring Senator Martin Warren's Office, Uncle Richard's Live Beacon News Takedown, Forcing a Ballot Against Charles Schuman, Bret Halverson's Premature Pentagon Victory Lap, & VPOTUS Conrad Drayton's Fury in S-216

summary: Behind-the-scenes look at Katie's primary upset over the DSCC, Uncle Richard defending her on Beacon News, her public No vote against Leader Charles Schuman, Defense Secretary Bret Halverson's premature 211–204 impeachment escape, the three-member Senate Wheelchair Caucus, and S-216.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 10, Chapter 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/across-the-rotunda-the-senate-of-virginia/the-accessibility-project-riding-every-bus-across-the-commonwealth-for-the-united-states-senate/part-3-the-roanoke-express-the-brooks-family-compound-on-lee-highway-the-maroon-express-to-bluewater-winning-the-june-primary) and [***Episode 11, Chapters 1–4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-senator-from-virginia/election-night-the-decision-desk-call-the-referendum-mandate/part-4-opposing-leader-schuman-the-211-204-lame-duck-false-dawn-in-the-dirksen-basement-home-across-the-fenwick-bridge), forty-one-year-old **State Senator Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia Beach`)** and her twin brother **Nate** ride public buses across every region of Virginia (`The Accessibility Project`), defeat `$14 million` establishment frontrunner and McLean venture capitalist businessman **Preston Holloway** in the June 2026 Democratic Primary (`55.6%` to `44.4%`), win the November 2026 General Election (`54.6%`), shake up the December lame-duck transition, and take the oath of office in the **120th Congress** on Sunday, January 3, 2027. This Backstage dossier reveals what happened behind the curtain in Washington, Richmond, and Danville.

---

## 1. The DSCC & Retiring Senator Martin Warren's Office (`January–June 2026`)

When retiring three-term **U.S. Senator Martin Warren (`D-Virginia`)** announced in January 2026 that he would not seek re-election, the **Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (`DSCC`)** on Capitol Hill and McLean venture capitalist businessman **Preston Holloway's** consultants in McLean treated the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary as a coronation:

1. **The `"Polite Token Challenger"` Misreading:**
   When Katie filed her `10,000+` verified voter signatures (`collected at bus transfer centers and train stations across all eleven congressional districts`) and announced she would campaign statewide exclusively by public transit alongside Nate without hiring a single D.C. media consultant, Holloway's team didn't even run negative ads against her—assuming a forty-one-year-old state senator in a power wheelchair riding county mountain buses was merely running to highlight transit funding before endorsing Holloway in June.
2. **Why *The Accessibility Project* Broke Holloway's Turnout Model:**
   What the DSCC consultants missed—because their models only polled high-propensity suburban drivers—was that Katie and Nate's live-blogged **Accessibility Project** (`fixing jammed wheelchair lifts on camera, riding the Maroon Express into Bluewater, visiting the Brooks family compound off Lee Highway, and wearing the National Firearms Association's 'F' grade as a badge of honor in Fairfax`) went viral in every rural county and urban bus corridor in Virginia. When Katie defeated Holloway **`55.6%` to `44.4%`** on June 16, 2026, Holloway's high-priced McLean media consultants were left staring in stunned silence at a fourteen-million-dollar self-funded and Super PAC ad buy that had been beaten across all eleven congressional districts by two siblings on a two-dollar bus pass.

---

## 2. Wednesday Morning, November 4, 2026 (`7:10 AM`): President Garrett Thorne's Meltdown & Uncle Richard on *Beacon News*

At `6:14 AM` on Wednesday, November 4, 2026—nine hours after every network Decision Desk called the Virginia U.S. Senate race for **Senator-Elect Katie Prairie (`54.6%` to `44.8%`)** alongside Virginia's **`61.4%` School Construction & Transit Referendum**—lame-duck **President Garrett Thorne** posted an all-caps tirade attacking *"BROKEN KATIE PRAIRIE, WHO CANNOT EVEN WALK OR STAND FOR OUR GREAT NATIONAL ANTHEM AND STOLE THE ELECTION IN VIRGINIA WITH PHONY BUS VOTES!"*

Katie and Nate ignored the post and ate breakfast in their Kempsville kitchen on Lord Nelson Drive.

Down in **Danville, Virginia**, however, retired **Former House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway (`R-Danville`)** saw the President's post over his morning coffee, picked up his phone, and booked himself live at `7:10 AM` on conservative cable flagship ***Beacon News Morning*** (`with his twenty-four-year-old niece and nephews Sarah, Mandy, and Sam Hawkins watching from their group chat`):

> *"Listen to me very carefully,"* Uncle Richard told the stunned *Beacon News* anchors from his living room in Danville. *"I served as the Republican Majority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates alongside Katie Prairie and her brother Nate. I disagreed with Katie on plenty of tax and spending bills, and she beat my caucus fair and square when she flipped the Seventh Senate District. Watching the President of the United States mock a woman in a wheelchair because she can't stand up for the National Anthem isn't conservatism—it's pathetic, cowardly trash. And as for her votes? Katie Prairie won fifty-four-point-six percent of the Commonwealth of Virginia because she and her brother rode every dusty bus route in Southwest and Southside Virginia that Washington politicians can't even find on a map!"*

---

## 3. Inside the Capitol Cabinet Shop: Preparing the Chamber for the Three-Member U.S. Senate Wheelchair Caucus (`November–December 2026`)

When the **120th United States Congress** convened on Sunday, January 3, 2027, the **Architect of the Capitol's** historic woodworking shop had just completed the largest accessibility upgrade to the Senate Chamber floor since **Senator Tess Dunmore (`D-Illinois`)** first entered the Senate:

* **Two Incoming Freshman Democrats in Wheelchairs (`Katie Prairie` & `Josh Novak`):**
  As shown in the November 2026 Senate Democratic freshman orientation reception in the Capitol, the incoming class of Democratic Senators-Elect included **two** full-time wheelchair users:
  1. **Senator-Elect Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia`):** Seated in her compact silver-and-black motorized **`SwiftChair`** power wheelchair (before hand-delivering her Virginia State Senate resignation in Richmond on December 15, 2026 under `Article IV, Section 4` of the Constitution of Virginia).
  2. **Senator-Elect Joshua "Josh" Novak (`D-Iowa`):** A forty-seven-year-old two-time Paralympic wheelchair basketball gold medalist and former Iowa State Representative from Council Bluffs born with spina bifida who used an ultralight black **`ApexLite`** manual wheelchair, positioned front-and-center alongside Katie in the freshman class portrait.
* **Joining Senior Wheelchair User Senator Tess Dunmore (`D-Illinois`):**
  Together with combat-wounded Iraq War Army helicopter pilot **Senator Teresa "Tess" Dunmore (`D-Illinois`)**—who had fought for the chamber's permanent well ramp and Presiding Officer rostrum lift in 2017—the 120th Senate featured a historic **three-member Senate Wheelchair Caucus**. Prior to January 3, 2027, the Architect of the Capitol's cabinetmakers unbolted the fixed pedestals at two outer-aisle 1819 mahogany Senate desks, fitting Senator Prairie's desk with `1.5-inch` solid Honduras mahogany riser blocks for her upright `SwiftChair` joystick and widening the rear staff bay by `38 inches` so Nate's `SwiftChair` could park right beside her left wheel without scratching a single square inch of the historic veneer.

---

## 4. Tuesday, December 1, 2026: Forcing a Ballot Against `Leader Charles Schuman` & Why the `211–204` Halverson Referral Backfired on the Pentagon

When Congress returned from the Thanksgiving recess on **Tuesday, December 1, 2026** ([***Episode 11, Chapter 1, Part 4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-senator-from-virginia/election-night-the-decision-desk-call-the-referendum-mandate/part-4-opposing-leader-schuman-the-211-204-lame-duck-false-dawn-in-the-dirksen-basement-home-across-the-fenwick-bridge)), two separate procedural clashes on opposite sides of the Capitol quietly set the entire chessboard for the **120th Congress**:

1. **Why `Senator Charles Schuman (D-New York)` Never Crossed Katie Again After the `43–11` Caucus Ballot:**
   Inside the closed doors of the **Mansfield Room (`S-207`)**, seventy-six-year-old **Senator Charles Schuman (`D-New York`)** expected to be re-elected incoming Senate Majority Leader by unanimous voice acclamation. Instead, Katie objected from her `SwiftChair`, forced a secret paper ballot (`43–11`, joined by **Senator-Elect Josh Novak** and nine other reform-minded Senators calling for generational change alongside incoming House **Speaker-Designate Clara Morales**), and rolled directly out to the hallway microphones to put her `"No"` vote on the public record. Behind closed doors afterward, DSCC operatives quietly asked **Appropriations Chairman Arthur Harrington** whether Katie's freshman subcommittee slots should be "reviewed." Harrington laughed in their faces—pointing out that Katie had just beaten their `$14 million` McLean recruit by eleven points without taking a dime of their money, and that Schuman needed Katie's vote on a `54–46` floor far more than Katie needed the DSCC. From that morning forward, Leader Schuman treated the junior Senator from Virginia with cautious, unmistakable deference.
2. **The Constitutional Trap Hidden Inside the House's `211–204` Motion to Refer:**
   That same afternoon—while Katie, Nate, and newly hired staffers **Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins** worked out of their cramped, windowless **Dirksen Basement Transition Cubicle (`Room SD-B14`)**—lame-duck **House Speaker Paul Jennings (`R-Louisiana`)** rescued **Secretary of Defense Bret Halverson** from outgoing Kentucky **Representative Thomas Mayfield's** eight privileged articles of impeachment by moving to refer the resolution to the outgoing House Judiciary Committee (`211–204`, aided by `18` absent lawmakers across both parties, with Mayfield casting the lone Republican `"Nay"` vote against burying his resolution). Ten minutes later, Halverson stepped into the Pentagon briefing room for the first time in six months and declared **"total victory."** Behind the scenes at the Pentagon, that seven-vote procedural escape proved fatal to the Thorne administration:
   - Had Mayfield's snap impeachment passed in forty-eight hours during the December lame-duck session without committee hearings, Senate defense lawyers could have attacked the record as rushed and uninvestigated.
   - Instead, convinced by his December 1 victory lap that he was untouchable, Halverson spent December recklessly texting classified **Naval Station Norfolk / Fifth Fleet** carrier deployment schedules over a commercial messaging group chat and firing the Pentagon Inspector General to hide `$400 million` in offshore fleet-supply contracts—handing the newly sworn-in **120th Congress** an airtight subpoena trail in January 2027!

---

## 5. What Happened Inside `S-216` When Katie Forced Vice President Conrad Drayton to Swear Her In on the U.S. Constitution (`January 3, 2027`)

In the main novel ([***Episode 11, Chapter 3, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-senator-from-virginia/first-train-from-norfolk-swearing-in-on-the-constitution-strings-attached-for-rrc/part-2-the-yellow-line-over-the-fenwick-bridge-the-full-chair-portrait-swearing-in-on-the-constitution)), readers see **Vice President Conrad Drayton** freeze for two seconds during the ceremonial photo re-enactment in the **Old Senate Chamber** when Katie holds out a leather-bound **pocket Constitution of the United States** instead of a Bible, and when the official Senate photographer lowers the tripod to frame Katie's full `SwiftChair` alongside **Nate** and **David**.

What happened ten minutes later when Vice President Drayton retreated into the **Vice President's Room (`S-216`)** off the Senate lobby?

1. **Why Drayton Couldn't Refuse (`Article VI, Clause 3`):**
   Behind the closed door of `S-216`, Drayton raged to his Chief of Staff that Katie Prairie had *"ambushed"* him for the cameras. His own Senate Parliamentarian liaison had to remind him gently that under **Article VI, Clause 3 of the United States Constitution** (*"no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States"*), a Senator-Elect has the absolute constitutional right to take the oath of office on a copy of the Constitution—and that **John Quincy Adams** had taken the Presidential Oath of Office on a volume of constitutional law in 1825.
2. **The Two Photographs That Went Viral Anyway:**
   Even worse for Drayton's press shop, the official Senate Photo Historian released the uncropped wide-angle portrait that evening showing **Senator Katie Prairie** in her full `SwiftChair` with her left hand on the **United States Constitution** held by **Nathaniel Prairie** in his `SwiftChair`, their father **David Prairie** standing beaming behind their push-handles, and a tight-jawed **Vice President Conrad Drayton** forced by constitutional duty to raise his right hand and administer the oath to the exact woman President Thorne had called *"Broken Katie Prairie"* eight weeks earlier.

> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 11, Chapter 5***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-senator-from-virginia/street-clothes-on-the-route-250-connector-unannounced-in-fishersville-calling-the-governor/arts-train-51-to-staunton-street-clothes-on-the-route-250-connector-calling-governor-langford-from-fishersville), readers are right inside the front visitor sign-in lobby of the **Bates-Harding Building** in Fishersville beside **Nathaniel Prairie** and **U.S. Senator Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia`)** in their `SwiftChair` power wheelchairs as Katie places a direct `9:22 AM` speakerphone call to **Virginia Governor Rebecca Langford (`D`)** and **Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence**. Over the speakerphone, Governor Langford announces that Arthur has just summoned **DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling** and the **Secretary of Health and Human Resources** across **Capitol Square** in ten minutes—and vows that anyone whose signature is on a false compliance certification to Congress will have their resignation on her desk before `5:00 PM`. This Backstage dossier opens the closed mahogany doors on the third floor of the **Patrick Henry Building** in Richmond twenty minutes later. --- ## 1. Thirty-Seven Minutes of Blind Panic in Richmond (`9:03 AM – 9:40 AM`) Until nine-oh-three on Thursday morning, July 22, 2027, **DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling** genuinely believed he had outsmarted the United States Senate. Forty-eight hours earlier (`Tuesday, July 20`), Sterling had couriered two identical eighty-four-page white comb-bound reports out of Richmond: 1. One copy up `I-95` to **Dirksen Room 511** and the **Senate Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education Appropriations Subcommittee**, certifying in bold 14-point type that all five of Senator Prairie's February 17 statutory mandates had reached *"Substantial Phase-One Implementation"* ahead of the following Thursday's FY2028 Subcommittee markup; and 2. A matching copy across Richmond with a two-page executive transmittal memo to **Secretary of Health and Human Resources Dr. Miriam Alcott** and **Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence**, assuring the **Governor's Office** that Fishersville had turned the corner so the Governor's Washington federal-relations office could lobby Senate Appropriations to lift Katie's **`\$18.5 million`** hold. Then, at **`9:03 AM`**, the direct administrative line from Fishersville lit up on the desk of Sterling's Deputy Commissioner: * Speaking in a breathless whisper behind the glass reception window of the **Bates-Harding Building** while **Director Evelyn Cross** and **Assistant Director Greg Saunders** escorted two black motorized `SwiftChair` power wheelchairs past the inner security podium, the Fishersville front-desk receptionist dropped a bomb on Richmond: > *"United States Senator Katie Prairie and her twin brother just rolled off the eight-thirty Route 250 bus in jeans and t-shirts! Nobody knew they were in Augusta County! They watched a Barton Hall resident get a yellow Level 2 pass time-stamped at our window, pulled an October 2019 handbook off the lobby rack, and slid two ordinary Virginia Beach DMV State ID cards under the glass—our receptionist didn't even recognize her name and told them Barton Hall still puts adult relatives in separate wings on Level 2 passes right before Dr. Cross walked in the front door at nine o'clock and recognized her! Now they're wearing clip-on visitor badges and Dr. Cross is escorting their wheelchairs down to the VITA-locked computer lab and Vocational Evaluation right now!"* For the next twenty minutes (`9:04 AM – 9:24 AM`), DARS executive headquarters descended into pandemonium: * Sterling bolted down the hall into his conference room, frantically coaching his deputy on hold with Fishersville while trying to reach **Secretary Miriam Alcott's** scheduler to "pre-spin" why an unannounced visit might catch *"transitional legacy forms still in physical circulation."* * At **`9:24 AM`**, while Sterling's deputy was still talking into the phone, the Fishersville receptionist whispered *"Oh God—she just told Dr. Cross to hang up on DARS and pulled out her cell phone"*—and the line went dead. * Fifteen minutes later, at **`9:39 AM`**, Secretary Miriam Alcott's private direct phone from **Capitol Square** rang once. It was **Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence**: > *"Miriam, Senator Katie Prairie and her brother are sitting in their wheelchairs in the front visitor lobby at Fishersville with Dr. Cross in front of them right now, and the Governor and I just spent seventeen minutes on speakerphone listening to Nate Prairie read your agency's Tuesday compliance binder back to us line by line against what is sitting on RRC's front counter. Walk across the Lawn to the Third Floor of the Patrick Henry Building with Marcus Sterling right now. Not on TeleGrid. Not in thirty minutes. Ten minutes."* --- ## 2. Inside the Governor's Working Office: Why Governor Rebecca Langford Was Volcanically IRATE (`9:50 AM – 10:15 AM`) When a pale, sweating **Commissioner Marcus Sterling** and a stunned **Secretary Dr. Miriam Alcott** were ushered past two Virginia Capitol Police troopers into the **Governor's Third-Floor Working Office** in the **Patrick Henry Building** at **`9:51 AM`**, **Governor Rebecca Langford** did not invite either of them to sit down. Standing behind her mahogany conference table in crisp navy sleeves—with **Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence** already holding his leather travel briefcase by the side door and **Governor's Chief Counsel David Halpern** seated beside an open laptop—Governor Langford wasn't merely frustrated by a bureaucratic misstep. She was **coldly, volcanically irate**, for four reasons she laid directly across the table without raising her voice above an iron-edged alto: 1. **Someone in Her Own Administration Had Lied to Virginia's United States Senator—And Specifically to Katie Prairie:** Rebecca Langford had served alongside Katie in Richmond during Katie's years in the **Senate of Virginia** and campaigned shoulder-to-shoulder with Katie and Nate across Hampton Roads and Northern Virginia in 2025 and 2026. > *"Of all the one hundred members of the United States Senate you could have tried to slip eighty-four pages of bureaucratic smoke past, Marcus,"* Governor Langford said, her voice shaking with controlled fury, *"you tried to lie to Katie Prairie! A fellow Democrat fighting tooth and nail on the Senate Appropriations Committee to bring healthcare, transit, and disability funding home to this Commonwealth—and the single most literal, detail-obsessed human being ever elected to public office in Virginia! A woman who reads every footnote of every budget rider alongside her twin brother on the train!"* 2. **Sterling Had Used the Governor's Own Office to Launder a False Certification to Congress:** Dropping Sterling's signed **July 20 Executive Transmittal Memo** onto the mahogany tabletop, Langford pointed straight at his blue-ink signature at the bottom: > *"You didn't just send a dishonest report to Dirksen Room 511. On Tuesday afternoon you walked into Miriam's Secretariat and sent my Chief of Staff a signed memorandum swearing up and down that Fishersville had completed Phase One—asking MY Washington office to pick up the phone to Senate Appropriations and vouch for your word! If Katie and Nate hadn't paid twenty-five cents apiece on a Shenandoah Valley bus this morning, you would have made the Governor of Virginia an accomplice to lying to the United States Congress!"* 3. **The Smoking-Gun `June 14, 2027` Email Pulled by the Governor's Counsel (`"Run Out the Clock Until Markup"`):** Before Sterling could stammer his rehearsed excuse—*"Governor, 'Substantial Phase-One Implementation' was intended as an administrative milestone reflecting our chartered 2028 Stakeholder Working Groups"*—Chief Counsel David Halpern turned his laptop screen forty-five degrees and slid a printed sheet from the Commonwealth's enterprise mail archive across the table. Seventeen minutes earlier, while Katie was still on speakerphone in Fishersville, Halpern and **VITA Chief Information Officer Rajiv Patel** had run a legal-hold search across Sterling's executive sent-items folder: > **From:** Marcus Sterling, Commissioner, Department for Aging and Rehabilitative Services
> **To:** Dr. Evelyn Cross, Director, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center
> **Cc:** Greg Saunders, Assistant Director, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center
> **Date:** Monday, June 14, 2027, 4:42 PM EDT
> **Subject:** Re: FY28 Subcommittee Hold & Handbook Working Group Timeline
>
> Evelyn — Keep the residential pass revision and Voc Eval curriculum waiver parked inside the Q1 2028 Stakeholder Working Group charters for the July transmittal binder. Do NOT pull the 2019 Barton Hall handbook or alter intake rotations prior to the July 29 Senate Labor-HHS Subcommittee markup. Once the FY28 bill clears Subcommittee markup next month, Dirksen 511's hold leverage expires until next spring and we can pace implementation internally.
> — M.S. Every drop of blood drained from Secretary Miriam Alcott's face as she read Sterling's own words over his shoulder. That single paragraph obliterated any pretense of an innocent misunderstanding: Sterling had deliberately ordered Fishersville to leave the abusive rules in place while certifying compliance to Congress to trick Senator Prairie into releasing **`\$18.5 million`**. 4. **Exposing the Entire Commonwealth to `\$92+ Million` in Federal Title I Sanctions & `18 U.S.C. § 1001` Scrutiny:** As Chief Counsel Halpern reminded the room icily, **Senate Appropriations Chairman Arthur Harrington** had already referred DARS to the federal **Rehabilitation Services Administration (`RSA`)** and **HHS Office for Civil Rights (`OCR`)** back on February 17. Submitting a knowingly false written compliance certification to a committee of the United States Congress to unlock **`\$18.5 million`** in federal funds brushed directly against the **Federal False Statements Act (`18 U.S.C. § 1001`)** and risked getting the entire Commonwealth designated a **`34 C.F.R. § 361` High-Risk Grantee**—endangering more than **`\$92 million`** in statewide federal vocational-rehabilitation matching funds for tens of thousands of disabled Virginians who had nothing to do with Fishersville's arrogance. --- ## 3. Two Folders on the Mahogany Table (`10:15 AM – 10:25 AM`): Firing vs. Resignation, Secretary Alcott's Final Warning, & Naming Acting Commissioner Thornton At **`10:14 AM`**, **Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence** checked his watch, picked up his briefcase to walk downstairs to the waiting state SUV with **State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton** and **VITA CIO Rajiv Patel**, and paused at the door just long enough to watch Governor Langford close the loop. Governor Langford laid **two manila folders** side by side in front of Marcus Sterling: * **The Left Folder (`Voluntary Resignation Effective 5:00 PM`):** A three-line letter addressed to the Governor tendering his immediate, irrevocable resignation as Commissioner of DARS effective at **`5:00 PM` on Thursday, July 22, 2027**, waiving any transition stipend and vacating state property by noon. * **The Right Folder (`Formal Removal for Cause Under Va. Code § 2.2-106 & § 51.5-131`):** Under Virginia law, a gubernatorial agency head serves strictly *"at the pleasure of the Governor."* Inside the right folder was an already-drafted **Executive Order of Removal for Cause**, explicitly removing Marcus Sterling from office for *"Intentional Material Misrepresentation to the United States Senate Committee on Appropriations and the Governor of Virginia"*—which the Governor's press secretary would release at `5:01 PM` to *The Richmond Dispatch*, *The Tidewater Pilot*, and *The Potomac Post* alongside a formal evidentiary referral of his June 14 email to the **Office of the State Inspector General (`OSIG`)**. > *"You have three minutes to decide which piece of paper leaves this room at ten-twenty, Marcus,"* Governor Langford said quietly. *"If you sign the left page, you clean out your personal photographs under Capitol Police escort before noon, you never set foot in a Virginia state agency building again, and my press release at five o'clock states in one sentence that I demanded and accepted your resignation following an unannounced compliance inspection in Fishersville. If you make me sign the right page, every hospital board, university trusteeship, and consulting firm in America will read the formal Findings of Cause and your June fourteenth email on page one tomorrow morning."* With a visibly trembling right hand, Marcus Sterling uncapped his pen at **`10:22 AM`**, signed the three-line resignation letter, and walked out the side hallway between two Capitol Police officers without looking up. ### Why Secretary of Health & Human Resources Dr. Miriam Alcott Did *Not* Resign—And Got Something Much Tougher Instead Once the door clicked shut behind Sterling, **Secretary Dr. Miriam Alcott** stood stiffly across the table and spoke quietly: *"Governor, that transmittal passed through my Secretariat on Tuesday with my routing initials. If you want my resignation alongside his before five o'clock, you have it right now."* Governor Langford looked across the mahogany table at her Cabinet Secretary for five long seconds—and shook her head once: 1. **Why Alcott Survived:** Chief Counsel Halpern's email audit confirmed that Secretary Alcott had **not** signed the false certification to Congress, was **never** copied on Sterling's June 14 stall strategy, and had explicitly asked Sterling face-to-face in Tuesday's Cabinet prep whether Fishersville's handbooks and computer labs were live—receiving a flat lie from her Commissioner. 2. **The Scorching Final Warning:** Letting Alcott resign would have handed her an easy exit while leaving twelve health agencies leaderless during budget season. Instead, Langford delivered an ice-cold final warning: > *"Marcus lied to you once in February, Miriam, and you took his word a second time in July without putting a single Deputy Secretary unannounced on a bus or in a state car to check Fishersville with your own eyes—and it took a sitting United States Senator and her twin brother riding a twenty-five-cent valley route in jeans to do your Secretariat's oversight job for you. You don't get to resign today. You are going to own every single line of my Friday noon emergency executive directive, and if one single deadline slips between tomorrow at noon and the day Senator Prairie lifts her hold, you won't need to offer me a letter twice."* 3. **Elevating `Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton` (`10:25 AM`):** To take immediate operational command of DARS, Governor Langford bypassed RRC's entire residential chain of command and appointed twenty-two-year vocational-rehabilitation field veteran **Deputy Commissioner Angela Thornton**—a widely respected blind-and-community-rehabilitation reformer from DARS's community field services division who had fought for years to fund assistive technology and college IT credentials over sheltered workshops—putting Thornton directly into the state SUV beside **Arthur Lawrence** as it pulled onto **Interstate 64 West** toward Fishersville.

title: Majority Leader Callaway's Closed-Door Post-Mortem on HB 663 & The Pre-Floor Review That Never Happened
subtitle: What Uncle Richard Wished Delegate Martin Cobb Had Done Before Bringing His Bill to the Floor—and What Would Have Happened in Room 518 If He Had
location: House Majority Leader's Office, Virginia State Capitol & Room 518, General Assembly Building, Richmond, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 9, Chapter 3, Parts 1–2)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 1: Line 18 & A Question Across the Chamber
summary: Behind-the-scenes look inside Majority Leader Richard Callaway's office after Delegate Katie Prairie and the thirteen-year-old Hawkins triplets dismantled HB 663 on the House floor—plus the alternate pre-floor QA review in Room 518 that could have spared the patron his televised humiliation.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 9, Chapter 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-gentlewoman-from-virginia-beach-the-house-of-delegates/house-bill-663-live-on-meet-the-nation/part-1-line-18-seated-by-delegate-ronald-villa-on-the-floor-a-question-across-the-chamber), readers see the February 4, 2016 floor battle over **House Bill 663** (*the "anatomical sex bathroom bill"*) from **Nathaniel Prairie's** seat beside **Delegate Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia Beach`)** on the House floor—and watch **House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway (`R-Danville`)** defend Katie's point of parliamentary inquiry before moving to pass by `HB 663` for the day and re-refer it to the Committee on Rules to die. This Backstage dossier reveals what happened behind closed doors in Majority Leader Callaway's office thirty minutes after the gavel fell—and walks through what would have happened in `Room 518` if the bill's patron, **Delegate Martin Cobb (`R-Spotsylvania`)**, had actually let Katie and the triplets stress-test his draft before bringing it to the floor.

---

## 1. *"Gentleman, This Embarrassment Was Entirely Preventable"*

From **House Majority Leader Richard Callaway's** perspective—backed by twenty-four years of legislative instincts in the House of Delegates—what happened on the House floor on Thursday, February 4, 2016 was not *"Katie Prairie embarrassed one of my members."*

It was: ***"Gentleman, this embarrassment was entirely preventable."***

What infuriated both Majority Leader Callaway and **Speaker of the House William J. Harwell (`R-Stafford`)** was that **Delegate Martin Cobb** (`HB 663`'s patron, the Gentleman from Spotsylvania) had brought a bill onto the House calendar whose central operative concept (*"anatomical sex"*) collapsed under the very first implementation question—turning a partisan talking point into an institutional humiliation on live Capitol television (`WCVE`) and national late-night comedy (*Saturday Night Sketch*).

---

## 2. The Closed-Door Dressing-Down in the Majority Leader's Office (`1:45 PM`)

Thirty minutes after moving that the House pass by `HB 663` for the day and re-referring it to the **Committee on Rules** to die quietly, Majority Leader Callaway closed the heavy mahogany door of his Capitol office with Delegate Martin Cobb and Speaker William J. Harwell inside:

* **Callaway:** *"You should've put this draft in front of Katie before you ever dropped it in the hopper."*
* **Delegate Cobb:** *"Prairie would've opposed it!"*
* **Callaway:** *"Of course she would've opposed it! That's why you should've put it in front of her! In this building, you give your bill to the smartest person you know who is determined to kill it. If it survives her, you might actually have a statute."*
* Leaning across his desk, Callaway delivered the line that became legend among the Capitol committee clerks:
  > *"Better yet, you should've walked upstairs to Room 518 and given it to Katie and those three Pages who eat lunch with her every day—my thirteen-year-old niece and nephews, Sarah, Mandy, and Sam Hawkins. Because if three thirteen-year-olds eating sandwich quarters in Room 518 can immediately discover a question your legislation cannot answer, you sure as hell do not want to discover that while standing at your microphone on the House floor!"*

---

## 3. Canonical *"What If"*: If Delegate Cobb Had Submitted `HB 663` to the Prairie + Triplets Review Before It Reached the Floor

Majority Leader Callaway's retrospective frustration was 100% justified—because if `HB 663` had gone through a private **Prairie + Triplets Review** in `Room 518` before reaching the House calendar, Katie and the triplets would have identified its fatal implementation flaw in less than five minutes through the exact kind of literal questions adults skip when drafting messaging bills:

### Step A: The Four-Person Bill Review in `Room 518`
Katie hands a printed draft copy to **Sam**, **Mandy**, and **Sarah Hawkins** around the worktable in `Room 518`. Sarah gets to the operative language on Line 18 of Page 1 first:
* **Sarah:** *"Katie?"*
* **Katie:** *"Hmm?"*
* **Sarah:** *"How do they know?"*
* **Katie:** *"Know what?"*
* **Sarah:** *"If somebody's anatomical sex matches the bathroom."*
* *(Katie stops reading.)*

title: Across the James River in Hillside Court: Watching the 6:00 PM News & Holding the General Assembly Elevator
subtitle: How Cousin Brittany Saw Delegate Katie Prairie on Television Thursday Night, Rode JRTC Across the Manchester Bridge Without an Appointment, & Stuck Her Hand in the Closing Doors
location: Hillside Court (South Richmond), Manchester Bridge, & General Assembly Building Lobby (Ninth & Broad, Richmond, Virginia)
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 3)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 3: Hold the Elevator! & Reuniting With Cousin Brittany in Room 518
summary: What happened across the James River in Hillside Court on Thursday evening, February 4, 2016—before Nate and Katie's first-person camera catches Brittany holding open the General Assembly Building elevator at 1:15 PM on Friday.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** Because [***Katie & Nathaniel***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie) is locked strictly to **Nathaniel's** first-person point of view in Episode 9, Katie and Nate have no idea on Thursday night, February 4, 2016 that their estranged thirty-year-old maternal cousin **Brittany Fletcher** is living less than three miles south of Capitol Square across the James River—until Nate yells *"Hold the elevator!"* in the General Assembly Building lobby at `1:15 PM` on Friday, February 5 ([***Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-gentlewoman-from-virginia-beach-the-house-of-delegates/house-bill-663-live-on-meet-the-nation/part-3-hold-the-elevator-reuniting-with-cousin-brittany-in-room-518-friday-night-on-jrtc-route-6-why-nate-must-speak)). This Backstage dossier documents Thursday night in **Hillside Court** and Brittany's unscheduled Friday midday bus ride into Downtown Richmond.

---

## 1. Thursday, February 4, 2016 (`6:04 PM EST`) — `Hillside Court` & The Six-O'Clock News Shock

Two miles south of Downtown Richmond across the James River, tucked between Jefferson Davis Highway and Harwood Street in South Richmond, sat the brick low-rise rows of **Hillside Court** public housing.

On paper, Hillside Court was less than fifteen minutes by bus from Capitol Square. Psychologically, living south of the wide, cold expanse of the James River felt like living on another planet—especially when thirty-one-year-old **Tyler** kept the only car keys in his pocket, checked grocery receipts down to the penny, screamed whenever dinner was five minutes late, and reminded thirty-year-old **Brittany Fletcher** almost every week that she had burned every bridge back home in Virginia Beach fourteen years ago on New Year's Eve 2002. (Crucially, when Brittany had met Tyler four years earlier at a tire shop on Little Creek Road, she had **no idea** he was the exact same loudmouth senior from New Year's Eve 2002 who had stumbled down the Prairie hallway banging on Katie's locked bedroom door and maliciously lied to **Heather Collins** in senior homeroom on January 6, 2003 about who Nate was locked in that room with—because seventeen-year-old Brittany had been wasted in the living room that night and banned by Uncle David the next morning without ever hearing what happened in Heather's homeroom; otherwise she never would have started dating him in the first place. Only at `9:00 AM` on Saturday wedding morning—when the Richmond morning news replays Katie's Capitol clip panning past Nate in his wheelchair and Tyler laughs and brags about lying to Heather—will that sickening truth finally dawn on Brittany as the straw that breaks the camel's back, while Katie and Nate figure out who Tyler is the instant they lay eyes on him at the wedding in [***Part 4***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-gentlewoman-from-virginia-beach-the-house-of-delegates/house-bill-663-live-on-meet-the-nation/part-4-via-southside-plaza-speaking-up-at-the-altar-taking-brittany-to-meet-the-nation-left-onto-macgregory-street).)

At four minutes past six on Thursday evening, February 4, 2016—forty-one hours before a Saturday afternoon church wedding in South Richmond that Brittany didn't even want to walk down the aisle for—Tyler was still across the living room scrolling his phone when the Richmond six-o'clock local broadcast cut straight to its lead story from the State Capitol:

> *"—a fiery floor exchange in the House of Delegates this afternoon over House Bill 663, the controversial bathroom bill restricting public restrooms by 'anatomical sex,' after Virginia Beach Delegate Katie Prairie brought the House Chamber to a standstill with a single question for the bill's patron."*

Standing by the tiny kitchen counter with a dish towel in her hands, Brittany froze.

Behind her thin silver wire-rimmed oval glasses, her eyes locked onto the small television screen. She already knew Katie and Nate used motorized `SwiftChair` power wheelchairs—she had stood on the far side of the uncut `Lions Way` curb at Northwood High School in eleventh grade watching them load onto the yellow lift bus. What stole every ounce of breath from Brittany's lungs was *where* her thirty-year-old cousin was sitting: upright in a royal-blue tailored blazer on the green carpet of the Virginia House of Delegates, holding up two printed pages of legislation beneath the brass chandelier of Thomas Jefferson's Capitol and fearlessly staring down a powerful committee patron on live television.

*That's Katie!* Brittany's mind raced, her heart slamming against her ribs as she pressed a trembling hand over her mouth so Tyler wouldn't see her gasp. *That's my cousin!! What is she doing in the House of Delegates!?*

Even more than the shock of seeing Katie's title on the lower-third television chyron (`DEL. KATIE PRAIRIE, D-VIRGINIA BEACH`), something else hit Brittany right in the chest: Katie wasn't across the Chesapeake Bay or two hours down Interstate 64 anymore. For the winter session of the General Assembly, Katie—and wherever Katie was, Nate was guaranteed to be right beside her—was **right here in the City of Richmond**, just across the Manchester Bridge.

That night, lying awake staring at the ceiling while bruise marks from earlier in the week still ached beneath her flannel shirt, Brittany made up her mind. She didn't have an appointment, she didn't know if Katie or Nate would slam the door in her face after fourteen years, and she knew she couldn't call from the apartment while Tyler was around. Tomorrow while Tyler was clocked in at the shop on Midlothian Turnpike, she was getting on the bus.

---

## 2. Friday, February 5, 2016 (`12:32 PM EST`) — `JRTC Route 74` (`"Via Southside Plaza"`) Across the James River

How does an ordinary citizen without a lobbyist badge or a scheduled appointment actually meet a Virginia State Delegate during session?

* **The Normal Capitol Routine (and the Katie Prairie Exception):** In ninety-nine out of one hundred offices in the General Assembly Building, walking in cold without an appointment means signing a visitor log at the outer reception desk, speaking for three minutes with a twenty-three-year-old Legislative Aide, leaving a yellow message slip, and hoping for a form letter in March—whereas anyone who called `Room 518` when Katie was at her desk usually got startled out of their shoes because Katie answered her own phone directly (*"Delegate Katie Prairie's office, this is Katie speaking"*).
* **Why Brittany Couldn't Call Ahead:** Calling from Southside risked missing Katie while she was down on the House Floor for the noon session—or losing her nerve completely if a staffer asked what bill number she was calling about. If she was going to beg for her life back, she had to look Katie and Nate in the eye.

At `12:32 PM` on Friday afternoon, wearing her dark winter coat over a plum sweater, jeans, and sneakers with her worn shoulder purse clutched against her side, Brittany stood at the Harwood Street bus stop outside Hillside Court as a blue-and-white forty-foot **`JRTC`** (*James River Transit Corporation*) low-floor bus rounded the corner heading inbound toward Downtown Richmond.

Anyone who ever rode transit south of the James River in Richmond knew **`JRTC`'s** unmistakable Southside obsession: making dead sure every single passenger on the sidewalk knew whether a bus was routing through **`Southside Plaza`** (`the massive mid-century Belt Boulevard & Hull Street transfer hub`). Above the windshield, the amber LED headsign flashed in alternating two-second frames—

> `74 OAK GROVE — DOWNTOWN`  
> `VIA SOUTHSIDE PLAZA`

—and the moment the folding front doors hissed open at the curb, the external speaker boomed across the block:

> *"Route 74. Downtown — via Southside Plaza. Welcome aboard JRTC!"*

Dropping exact change into the farebox, Brittany sat near the middle window with both hands knotted tightly in her lap as `Route 74` climbed out of Southside, rolled up Commerce Road onto the high steel deck of the **Manchester Bridge (`Ninth Street Bridge`)** high above the rocky rapids of the James River, and glided straight up Ninth Street to the brick sidewalk outside Capitol Square.

---

## 3. Friday, February 5, 2016 (`1:08 PM – 1:15 PM EST`) — Clearing Security, `Room 518`, & *"Hold the Elevator!"*

Stepping off the bus into the crisp February wind at Ninth and Broad, Brittany stared up at the towering limestone facade of the General Assembly Building.

For three full minutes she stood frozen by the curb, half convinced Capitol Police would ask why someone from Hillside Court without a suit jacket or an appointment calendar belonged inside. Taking one shaky breath, she walked through the heavy glass doors into the ground-floor security vestibule, set her purse into the gray plastic bin on the X-ray conveyor belt, and stepped cleanly through the metal detector archway.

"Have a good afternoon, ma'am," the Capitol Police officer said politely, sliding her purse down the rollers.

Brittany stepped past the stanchion into the high-ceilinged marble lobby and had to stop beside a fluted column just to catch her breath.

*She was in the General Assembly Building. She had actually done it.*

Steadying her glasses with two cold fingers, she walked up to the tall glass-framed legislative directory mounted beside the information desk and scanned down the alphabetical column of House members until her finger stopped on a single white plastic strip:

> `PRAIRIE, KATIE — 85TH DISTRICT — ROOM 518`

*Fifth floor,* Brittany told herself, swallowing hard as she looked left toward the gleaming brass doors of the main elevator bank. *Okay. Relax, Brittany. Elevators are right over there. Just go up to five, tell the receptionist you're her cousin from Virginia Beach, and if Katie tells you to leave, you walk quietly back down to the bus stop and go.*

Her knees feeling like water, she walked across the polished marble floor and pressed the brass `UP` call button.

Ten seconds later, a soft bell chimed above the right-hand shaft. The heavy brass doors slid open onto an empty wood-paneled elevator cab. Brittany stepped inside alone, clutched her purse strap with both hands like a lifeline—a complete nervous wreck—and watched the brass doors begin sliding smoothly shut, narrowing her view of the marble lobby down to a six-inch gap.

Right across the lobby echo came a young man's voice shouting at the top of his lungs:

***"HOLD THE ELEVATOR!"***

Pure reflex moved before Brittany's brain could catch up—thrusting her left hand straight between the closing brass doors to trigger the rubber safety edge and pop them wide open again, bringing her face-to-face with two compact black-and-silver `SwiftChair` power wheelchairs rolling straight toward the threshold.

Pure reflex moved before Brittany's brain could catch up—thrusting her left hand straight between the closing brass doors to trigger the rubber safety edge and pop them wide open again, bringing her face-to-face with two compact black-and-silver SwiftChair power wheelchairs rolling straight toward the threshold.
