Welcome to the official **RaggieSoft Backstage** companion archive for [***Katie & Nathaniel***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie).

Because every chapter of ***Katie & Nathaniel*** is written strictly in **Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view**, the main novel only shows what Nate and Katie can directly see, hear, and deduce in the moment. Whenever you encounter a **Backstage Bonus Feature** button at the end of a chapter on [`books.raggiesoft.com`](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie), you can open these behind-the-scenes dossiers directly inside the reader without breaking narrative immersion.

---

## Complete Chronological Index of Behind-the-Scenes Dossiers (`2001–2044`)

1. [**Oct 19, 2001 — The Sunward Tropics Security File & How Brenda Lost the 'Prairie' Surname**](/books/katie/sunward-tropics-divorce-and-maiden-name-order)
   What happened behind closed doors when Brenda's attorney walked into Arthur Vance's conference room off Independence Boulevard to watch the *M/S Sunward Tropics* Deck 4 security tape—and how Katie and Nate's request forced Brenda to sign the `Va. Code § 20-121.4` stipulation surrendering the `Prairie` family name and reverting to **`Brenda Walsh`**.
2. [**Oct 16–20, 2004 — CBSA Secondary Inspection at 35 Park Street East & The U.S. Marshals File on Brandon Mercer**](/books/katie/cbsa-windsor-tunnel-refusal-and-marshals-file)
   Reconstructs what happened between nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate's `4:00 PM` six-bus escape from the Williamsburg Transportation Center and Brandon Mercer's arrest by Deputy U.S. Marshals at a men's shelter on **Cass Avenue** in Detroit—including his ripped-up ticket on **East Jefferson Avenue**, the Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus farebox trap, his refusal of entry into Canada at **`555 Goyeau Street`** and **`35 Park Street East`** in Windsor, Ontario, and the CBP seizure of his two contraband hard drives on **Randolph Street**.
3. [**Dec 24–27, 2004 — Dirty Old Tonomy Hill & Why Brandon's Tunnel-Bus Scheme Was Doomed Before He Left Williamsburg**](/books/katie/christmas-2004-tonomy-hill-and-williamsburg-what-if)
   Why developmentally disabled **Cousin Chelsea** actually held the sole legal authority on the Newport Housing Authority lease to evict Tiffany Sloan from her apartment on Tonomy Hill while locking Katie and Nate safely inside her bedroom—plus the two rail and cross-border bus tariff rules Brandon Mercer never bothered to read before leaving Williamsburg.
4. [**Mar 8–15, 2007 — The Unopened RRC Staff Dossier: Form A vs. Form B & The Unsigned Level 1 Contract**](/books/katie/rrc-staff-file-voc-eval-and-level-1-contract)
   Opens the internal Bates-Harding staff notes on `"Prairie, Nathaniel"` and `"Prairie, Katie"`—revealing why Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller separated their tests into `Form A` and `Form B` expecting them to cheat on the outdated 1996 exam battery, why `VITA` locked down the lab on `Quantum OS 2000 Professional`, and the drafted **`Level 1` Restriction & Mandatory Separation Contract** sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning.
5. [**Mar 13, 2007 — The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Seasonal Closet Door Got Nate and Katie Caught**](/books/katie/rrc-seasonal-closet-curfew-search)
   Discover how Barton Hall dorm staff tracked Nate and Katie to the Rec Hall without an on-campus sign-out sheet—and why locking a normally unlocked door in a notorious student hookup closet is the exact thing that tipped the night supervisor off while the twins were hidden in the dark.
6. [**Mar 14–15, 2007 — How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Morning Cover-Up**](/books/katie/rrc-dorm-database-hack-and-coverup)
   What happened behind closed doors when Christopher Vance stole an open administrative login to swap opposite-gender dorm room assignments on Wednesday night, why RRC whisked him onto a bus in Staunton at `7:50 AM` on Thursday without calling the State Police, and why Nate and Katie's `10:00 AM` `Level 1` disciplinary counselor meeting never happened.
7. [**Oct 28, 2010 — The 509 East 18th Street Executive Suite, Mayor Overton's Bus, & Harold Dietz's 0.4% Collapse**](/books/katie/mayor-overton-newtown-road-and-2010-dietz-meltdown)
   Why CVTA CEO Leonard Sterling and COO Richard Halstead blackballed Nate from `TRAC`, the real Tidewater municipal history of the Newtown Road bus-border cliff that haunted Mayor Myra E. Overton, why Incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz left his debate podium empty on `WHRC TV-15`, and the internal tracking poll (`44.6%` to `44.2%`) that triggered his fatal `WTGA 790 AM` radio attack on Katie's wheelchair ramp.

   What happened inside **House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway's (`R-Danville`)** Capitol office thirty minutes after `HB 663` imploded on the floor—and the step-by-step pre-floor bill review in `Room 518` with Katie and the thirteen-year-old Hawkins triplets (`Sarah`, `Mandy`, and `Sam`) that would have spared **Delegate Martin Cobb** his televised humiliation.

   Reveals how Uncle Richard Callaway and Aunt Marge rescued thirteen-year-old autistic triplets **Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins** in early 2015, why the triplets bolted from the doorway of `Room 518` during Katie and Nate's Friday morning meltdown to fetch both Floor Leaders, and how *Saturday Night Sketch* (`Studio 6B`) wrote the viral `HB 663` cold open without "cripping up."

    Inside retiring Senator Martin Warren's office and the DSCC when Katie and Nate's bus-riding campaign defeated Preston Holloway, Uncle Richard going live on *Beacon News* from Danville to defend Katie against President Garrett Thorne, Katie forcing a recorded `43–11` caucus ballot against **Senate Majority Leader Charles Schuman (`D-NY`)**, **Defense Secretary Bret Halverson's** premature *"total victory"* lap after escaping impeachment on a `211–204` lame-duck referral vote, the Architect of the Capitol's desk upgrades for the three-member **U.S. Senate Wheelchair Caucus** (`Senator Tess Dunmore [D-IL]`, `Senator Katie Prairie [D-VA]`, and `Senator Josh Novak [D-IA]`), and Vice President Conrad Drayton's fury in `S-216` over swearing Katie in on the U.S. Constitution.

    Follow the nine stages of bureaucratic collapse inside **Dirksen Room 511** as DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and RRC Director Evelyn Cross wonder how a United States Senator knows the exact color of 2007 `Level 2` Barton Hall passes, the `MedStrip` wound-closure strips on a girl's broken nose, and the lumpy bags of curtains inside a Rec Hall storage closet—until the math clicks (`41 - 20 = 21`) and Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence reads them the Riot Act from Richmond.
12. [**Jul 22, 2027 (9:03–10:25 AM) — Governor Langford's Capitol Square Reckoning With Commissioner Sterling & Secretary Alcott**](/books/katie/governor-langford-capitol-square-reckoning-with-sterling)
    What happened inside the **Patrick Henry Building** on **Capitol Square** twenty minutes after Katie called **Governor Rebecca Langford** on speakerphone from Fishersville—as a volcanically irate Governor confronts **DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling** and **Secretary of Health and Human Resources Dr. Miriam Alcott** with Sterling's June 14 *"wait out the July markup"* email, lays two manila folders (`5:00 PM Resignation` vs. `Va. Code § 2.2-106 Removal for Cause`) on her mahogany table, keeps Secretary Alcott on an ice-cold final warning, and elevates **Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton**.
13. [**Jul 22, 2027 (12:38–8:15 PM) — Arthur Lawrence's Fishersville Sweep, VITA's 120-Day Unsigned Form, & The 5:00 PM Resignations**](/books/katie/arthur-lawrence-fishersville-audit-and-five-oclock-resignations)
    Follow **Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence**, **State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton**, **VITA CIO Rajiv Patel**, and **Acting Commissioner Angela Thornton** up `I-64` into Fishersville at `12:38 PM`—uncovering VITA's approved March 24 classroom VLAN form that Dr. Cross left unsigned for 120 days, unlocking all twelve lab workstations live by `4:15 PM`, pulling lobby security video of **Assistant Director Greg Saunders** grabbing twenty-year-old Marcus's wheelchair push-handles alongside a June purchase order for 5,000 yellow passes, and securing Cross's and Saunders's resignations before `5:00 PM` in lieu of `Group III` termination.
14. [**Mar 2027 – Spring 2044 — Brenda Walsh's Suite 756 Cease-and-Desist, Thorne's Gag Order, & The 2044 Route 15 Bus-Stop Primary**](/books/katie/brenda-walsh-suite-756-and-the-2044-route-15-primary)
    The complete story behind **Brenda Walsh's** unauthorized *Tidewater Thorne & RTR Superstore* in **`Suite 756` at Timberline Shopping Center** (`shut down by a Cease-and-Desist letter from Thorne Enterprises ten days after her own daughter voted to convict and bar Garrett Thorne for life`), how a federal bail gag order (`18 U.S.C. § 3142`) silenced Thorne, and why fifty-eight-year-old three-term Senator Katie Prairie refused the **2044 Presidential Nomination** at the **CVTA Route #15** bus stop and forced every White House contender to interview on a live Virginia Beach transit loop (*"Wait—a bus? Huh?!"*).

location: 509 E. 18th Street, Norfolk, Virginia; WHRC TV-15 Studios & WTGA 790 AM Broadcast Booth, Virginia Beach, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 8, Chapters 1–2)

> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 8***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/do-better-ideas-for-cvta-the-kempsville-city-council/do-better-ideas-for-cvta-the-four-bus-mayoral-loop/part-1-does-the-bus-run-calling-out-cvta-s-complacency-the-2008-regional-mayoral-challenge), twenty-two-year-old **Katie** and **Nathaniel Prairie** turn their transit advocacy blog (*Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit*) and their May 2008 **"Ride the Bus With Us"** Mayoral Challenge into Katie's historic 2010 landslide campaign for the **Kempsville District** seat on the **Virginia Beach City Council**. This Backstage dossier reveals what happened behind closed doors at **CVTA Headquarters (`509 E. 18th Street`)** and inside twenty-two-year incumbent **Councilman Harold Dietz's** imploding war room.

---

## 1. Why CVTA Executive Leadership Blackballed Nate From `TRAC` (`2007–2010`)

When twenty-one-year-old **Nathaniel Prairie** submitted his application for the citizen **Transit Rider Advisory Committee (`TRAC`)** at **`509 E. 18th Street`** in Norfolk, **CVTA Chief Executive Officer Leonard Sterling** and **Chief Operating Officer Richard Halstead** personally flagged his file in the second-floor executive suite:

1. **They Wanted Compliant Ceremonial Riders, Not Software Engineers Reading the NTD Tables:**
   To Sterling and Halstead, `TRAC` existed to rubber-stamp staff fare-increase proposals and clap politely for glossy PowerPoint slides. The last thing they wanted at the advisory table was the co-author of *Ideas for Coastal Virginia Transit*—who was already publishing interactive route maps exposing how CVTA buses ran once every sixty minutes, stopped running at `7:00 PM`, and stranded wheelchair riders at un-signalized six-lane highway crossings without sidewalks.
2. **Cutting the Microphone at Two Minutes (`02:00`):**
   Whenever Nate and Katie rode two buses into Norfolk to speak during the public-comment period at monthly **Transportation District Commission (`TDC`)** board meetings, COO Halstead instructed the board clerk to start the digital countdown clock the instant their power wheelchairs began rolling toward the lectern—and cut their microphone dead at `02:00` sharp.
3. **The November 2010 Boomerang:**
   Neither Sterling nor Halstead ever imagined that blackballing the brother from a volunteer citizen committee in 2008 would result in the sister being elected to the **Virginia Beach City Council** with **`94.1%` of the vote** in November 2010—and appointed by the Mayor two months later as a **voting Commissioner on the CVTA Board of Directors**, where she sat on the raised dais above their heads with no two-minute clock and voted to clean house in the executive suite.

---

## 2. The Political Folklore of the Newtown Road Timetable Cliff & Mayor Myra E. Overton (`1988–2008`)

Why did the four-bus, three-hour loop on **May 14, 2008**—carrying Norfolk Mayor **Paulina Fraim**, Virginia Beach Mayor **Myra E. Overton**, and Portsmouth Mayor **James Holley** alongside Katie and Nate—strike such a raw nerve across Hampton Roads when their bus hit the Norfolk/Virginia Beach city line at **Newtown Road**?

* **The Invisible Municipal Wall at Newtown Road:**
  For decades, **CVTA Route #1** (`Granby Street / Pembroke East`) operated every `15–30 minutes` on the Norfolk side of the city line, while **CVTA Route #20 / #25** (`Virginia Beach Boulevard / Kempsville`) dropped to `60-minute` headways with uncoordinated transfer windows the instant a rider crossed Newtown Road into Virginia Beach.
* **Twenty Years of Saying *"Nobody Rides the Bus Out Here"*:**
  Throughout her twenty years in Virginia Beach municipal politics (`1988–2008`), **Mayor Myra E. Overton** had defended Virginia Beach's skeletal bus funding by claiming at budget hearings that *"suburban residents prefer their cars."* Having to sit in a rigid molded-fiberglass bus seat for forty-two minutes at the Newtown Road transfer stop in the May humidity while twenty-two-year-old Katie and Nate calmly pointed out on a printed schedule that a five-mile trip from Kempsville to City Hall required four hours and two transfers turned the **Newtown Road Timetable Cliff** into instant Tidewater political folklore.

---

## 3. Why Councilman Harold Dietz Left His Podium Empty on `WHRC TV-15`—and Blew Up His Career on `WTGA 790 AM` (`October 2010`)

How did twenty-two-year incumbent **Councilman Harold Dietz** go from a comfortable `+18%` summer lead to losing the Kempsville District **`94.1%` to `5.9%`** on November 2, 2010?

1. **Why Dietz Never RSVPed to the `WHRC TV-15` Debate (`October 19, 2010`):**
   When public television station **`WHRC TV-15`** sent certified debate invitations to both certified Kempsville candidates in September 2010, Dietz's campaign manager advised him to ignore the letter—assuming `WHRC TV-15` would cancel the broadcast if the incumbent didn't confirm, and refusing to *"elevate a twenty-five-year-old kid in a wheelchair who rides the city bus."*
   Instead, `WHRC TV-15` followed strict FCC *bona fide* news event rules: they set up two podiums under the studio lights, placed a `COUNCILMAN HAROLD DIETZ` nameplate on the empty lectern, and gave twenty-five-year-old **Katie Prairie** thirty uninterrupted minutes on live regional television—followed by *The Virginian-Pilot* front-page Metro photograph of Katie and Nate sprinting across four lanes of Independence Boulevard in the dark at `8:24 PM` to catch the last three buses home.
2. **The Internal Track Poll That Triggered the `WTGA 790 AM` Meltdown (`October 27–28, 2010`):**
   Six days after the `WHRC TV-15` broadcast and the front-page *Virginian-Pilot* story, Dietz's campaign pollster delivered a devastating internal tracking poll of 400 likely Kempsville voters:
   * **September 15, 2010:** Dietz `51%` — Prairie `33%` (`Dietz +18%`)
   * **October 12, 2010:** Dietz `46%` — Prairie `38%` (`Dietz +8%`)
   * **October 27, 2010 (*Post-Empty Podium*):** Prairie `44.6%` — Dietz `44.2%` (`Statistical Tie / Margin of Error 0.4%`)
3. **8:15 AM on `WTGA 790 AM` (*The Morning Drive with Chuck & Dave*):**
   Furious, panicked, and sleepless after seeing his twenty-two-year seat evaporate to a `0.4%` margin against a twenty-five-year-old challenger who hadn't bought a single television commercial, Dietz drove to the **`WTGA 790 AM`** studio on Thursday morning, October 28 without his campaign manager—and went on live talk radio to sneer that electing Katie Prairie would *"cost the taxpayers of Virginia Beach tens of thousands of dollars just to tear up the historic mahogany City Council dais at Building 1 to build a custom wheelchair ramp for one girl who doesn't even own a car."*
   Within four hours, every civic league president, military veteran, church pastor, and parent of a child with a disability in Kempsville had heard the clip—turning a `0.4%` race into the most lopsided City Council landslide (`94.1%`) in Virginia Beach history.

How did twenty-two-year incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz go from a comfortable +18% summer lead to losing the Kempsville District 94.1% to 5.9% on November 2, 2010?

  1. Why Dietz Never RSVPed to the WHRC TV-15 Debate (October 19, 2010):
    When public television station WHRC TV-15 sent certified debate invitations to both certified Kempsville candidates in September 2010, Dietz's campaign manager advised him to ignore the letter—assuming WHRC TV-15 would cancel the broadcast if the incumbent didn't confirm, and refusing to "elevate a twenty-five-year-old kid in a wheelchair who rides the city bus."
    Instead, WHRC TV-15 followed strict FCC bona fide news event rules: they set up two podiums under the studio lights, placed a COUNCILMAN HAROLD DIETZ nameplate on the empty lectern, and gave twenty-five-year-old Katie Prairie thirty uninterrupted minutes on live regional television—followed by The Virginian-Pilot front-page Metro photograph of Katie and Nate sprinting across four lanes of Independence Boulevard in the dark at 8:24 PM to catch the last three buses home.
  2. The Internal Track Poll That Triggered the WTGA 790 AM Meltdown (October 27–28, 2010):
    Six days after the WHRC TV-15 broadcast and the front-page Virginian-Pilot story, Dietz's campaign pollster delivered a devastating internal tracking poll of 400 likely Kempsville voters:
    • September 15, 2010: Dietz 51% — Prairie 33% (Dietz +18%)
    • October 12, 2010: Dietz 46% — Prairie 38% (Dietz +8%)
    • *October 27, 2010 (Post-Empty Podium):* Prairie 44.6% — Dietz 44.2% (Statistical Tie / Margin of Error 0.4%)
  3. *8:15 AM on WTGA 790 AM (The Morning Drive with Chuck & Dave):*
    Furious, panicked, and sleepless after seeing his twenty-two-year seat evaporate to a 0.4% margin against a twenty-five-year-old challenger who hadn't bought a single television commercial, Dietz drove to the WTGA 790 AM studio on Thursday morning, October 28 without his campaign manager—and went on live talk radio to sneer that electing Katie Prairie would "cost the taxpayers of Virginia Beach tens of thousands of dollars just to tear up the historic mahogany City Council dais at Building 1 to build a custom wheelchair ramp for one girl who doesn't even own a car."
    Within four hours, every civic league president, military veteran, church pastor, and parent of a child with a disability in Kempsville had heard the clip—turning a 0.4% race into the most lopsided City Council landslide (94.1%) in Virginia Beach history.

title: Why the House Page Triplets Bolted From Room 518 & How Uncle Richard Rescued Them
subtitle: The Story of Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins, Why Their Badges Didn't Match Majority Leader Callaway's Nameplate, & Inside Studio 6B at Saturday Night Sketch
location: Room 518, General Assembly Building, Richmond, Virginia; Danville, Virginia; & Studio 6B, Rockefeller Center, New York
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 2)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 2: Two Meltdowns in Room 518 & Page Forty-Two
summary: Behind-the-scenes backstory explaining why thirteen-year-old autistic House Page triplets Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins bolted from the doorway of Room 518 during Katie and Nate's Friday morning meltdown—plus how Saturday Night Sketch wrote the viral HB 663 cold open without 'cripping up.'
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 9, Chapter 3, Part 2***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/the-gentlewoman-from-virginia-beach-the-house-of-delegates/house-bill-663-live-on-meet-the-nation/part-2-transit-legislative-day-in-room-518-the-six-o-clock-news-two-meltdowns-answered-by-page-forty-two), Caucus Communications Director Greg's shouting in the fifth-floor outer office on Friday morning, February 5, 2016 triggers a simultaneous autistic meltdown in `Room 518` for **Delegate Katie Prairie** and **Nathaniel Prairie**—and thirteen-year-old House Page triplets **Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins** take one look inside the doorway and bolt down the corridor to fetch their uncle, **House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway (`R-Danville`)**, alongside **Minority Leader Tom Toscano (`D-Charlottesville`)**. This Backstage dossier reveals the triplets' backstory and what happened in New York City the next night at *Saturday Night Sketch*.

---

## 1. Why the Triplets' Page Badges Read `HAWKINS` While the Majority Leader's Desk Read `CALLAWAY`

Capitol visitors who saw thirteen-year-old eighth-grade House Pages **Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins** eating their crustless sandwich quarters in `Room 518` with **Delegate Katie Prairie (`D-Virginia Beach`)** every day at noon often had no idea that the three quiet kids in navy-blue Page blazers were the niece and nephews of the most powerful Republican on the House floor: **House Majority Leader Richard Callaway (`R-Danville`)**.

1. **Maternal Uncle & The Early-2015 Kinship Rescue:**
   Sam, Mandy, and Sarah (`born October 2002`) were the children of Majority Leader Richard Callaway's younger sister, **Jenny Callaway Hawkins**, and her ex-husband **Wayne Hawkins**. All three triplets were diagnosed on the autism spectrum in elementary school. In early 2015, after Wayne Hawkins abandoned the family and Jenny suffered a severe medical and financial crisis that left the twelve-year-old triplets facing an abusive, chaotic household where they were screamed at whenever they had sensory overload, **Richard Callaway** and his wife **Aunt Marge** drove across Pittsylvania County in a snowstorm, petitioned the Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court for permanent kinship custody, and brought all three triplets home to their farmhouse outside **Danville**.
2. **Why Uncle Richard Appointed Them to the House Page Class of 2016:**
   When the triplets turned thirteen in the fall of eighth grade, Uncle Richard and Aunt Marge arranged for all three of them to serve together in Richmond in the **House of Delegates Page Program** so they would never be separated during the sixty-day winter session—and privately asked **Delegate Katie Prairie** and **Nate** during the first week of January 2016 if the triplets could eat their quiet lunches inside `Room 518` away from the loud, echoey Capitol cafeteria.

---

## 2. Why Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Bolted From the Doorway of `Room 518` (`Friday, February 5, 2016, 9:40 AM`)

When the neighboring delegate's legislative assistant slammed open the door of `Room 518` and yelled at Katie and Nate over the ringing `Meet the Nation` phone line—triggering a full sensory-overload meltdown for both thirty-year-old twins—Sam, Mandy, and Sarah arrived at the open doorway with the `9:40 AM` floor packet.

To the mortified staffer in the hallway, it looked like three thirteen-year-old Pages had been frightened away by two crying adults in wheelchairs.

In reality, the exact opposite happened inside the triplets' heads:

* **Instant Autistic Recognition:**
  Being autistic themselves—and having spent the past year learning from Uncle Richard and Aunt Marge how to protect one another during sensory overload—Sam, Mandy, and Sarah recognized within half a second that Katie and Nate were having an **autistic meltdown caused by someone yelling at them in their safe space**.
* **Why They Didn't Step Inside `Room 518`:**
  The triplets knew from their own meltdowns that three more voices crowding into a small room would only make the sensory overload worse—and they also knew that three thirteen-year-old Pages didn't have the institutional authority to clear the fifth-floor hallway or lock down the corridor.
* **Straight to the One Adult Who Could Command the Building:**
  Without saying a word to the staffer, Sam, Mandy, and Sarah spun on their heels, sprinted down the marble stairs to the Majority Leader's suite, and burst straight past the reception desk to tell **Uncle Richard** (who immediately grabbed **Democratic Minority Leader Tom Toscano** down the hall):
  > *"Uncle Richard! Some jerk yelled at Katie and Nate in Room 518 and they're having a really bad meltdown and you have to go fix the hallway right now!"*
  Within three minutes, the Republican Majority Leader and the Democratic Minority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates were standing shoulder to shoulder outside `Room 518` like two bouncers while Sam, Mandy, and Sarah slipped quietly under the worktable to sit on the carpet with Katie and Nate until the room felt safe again.

---

## 3. Inside Studio 6B: How *Saturday Night Sketch* Wrote the Viral `HB 663` Cold Open (`Saturday, February 6, 2016`)

Thirty-six hours later, while Katie, Nate, and their newly rescued cousin **Brittany Fletcher** were safely locked inside `Apartment 104` at the **Broad & Boulevard Lofts** in Richmond ahead of Sunday morning's `6:05 AM` train to Washington for ***Meet the Nation*** on `GBS`, the writing room on the eighth floor of **30 Rockefeller Plaza (`Studio 6B`)** in New York City was rewriting the **Saturday Night Sketch** cold open from scratch:

1. **Scrapping the Presidential Primary Cold Open on Friday Afternoon:**
   Originally, the February 6, 2016 cold open was slated to be a standard New Hampshire primary debate sketch. Then the `WCVE` floor clip of thirty-year-old **Delegate Katie Prairie** asking **Delegate Martin Cobb** whether she would have to lift her skirt and pull down her pants in front of a police officer to prove her *"anatomical sex"* crossed `18 million` views on Friday afternoon.
2. **The Cast's Strict Rule: Parody the Bill and the Patron, Never "Crip Up" to Mock the Wheelchair User:**
   In the Friday night table read, head writer **Claire Montgomery** laid down a non-negotiable rule for the sketch: *Saturday Night Sketch* would **not** put an able-bodied cast member in a prop wheelchair (`"cripping up"`) to impersonate Katie Prairie—because Katie wasn't the punchline of the story; **the patron's unenforceable bill was the punchline**.
3. **The `"Department of Anatomical Verification"` Sketch (`11:30 PM EST`):**
   Instead, the six-minute cold open opened inside a fictional Virginia Capitol committee room where a flustered **"Delegate Cobb"** attempts to demonstrate his new `"Virginia Restroom Anatomical Verification Kiosk"`—complete with a bewildered Capitol Police sergeant holding a ruler, a birth certificate, a magnifying glass, and a stack of $50 civil-penalty tickets—while three deadpan thirteen-year-old House Pages (`played by the show's three youngest cast members`) raise their hands every ten seconds to ask literal software-QA questions (*"Sir, what if someone left their chromosomes in their other pants?"*) until the fictional Speaker drops a giant wooden gavel from the ceiling and yells: ***"Live from New York, it's Saturday Night!"***

title: How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Cover-Up
subtitle: Behind the Scenes of Wednesday Night's Keycard Swap & Why Thursday's Counselor Meeting Never Happened
location: Bates-Harding Building & Barton Hall, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center, Fishersville, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 6, Chapter 3, Parts 1–2)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 6, Chapter 3, Part 1: The Dormitory Room Mix-Up
summary: What happened outside Nate's first-person POV when Christopher Vance stole an open admin login to scramble the Barton Hall room database, and how RRC administration swept Natalie Brooks's assault under the rug on Thursday morning.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 6, Chapter 3***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/twelve-days-at-roosevelt-rehabilitation-center-walking-out-for-good/the-dormitory-room-mix-up-tina-s-daybed-in-luray-leaving-rrc-after-twelve-days/part-1-the-dormitory-room-mix-up-blind-red-tape-room-reassignments-a-sleepless-night-for-natalie), Nate and Katie experience Wednesday night, March 14, 2007 strictly from the Barton Hall hallway—where dorm staff blindly follow a scrambled computer printout assigning male and female students to opposite-gender rooms, Nate rescues Katie when **Christopher Vance (`Chris`)** shows up at her doorway, and they find **Natalie Brooks** sobbing outside the cafeteria on Thursday morning before learning Chris was quietly sent away. This Backstage dossier documents what happened behind closed doors in the RRC housing office and infirmary—facts that Nate and Katie only piece together in full twenty years later when Natalie's mother, **Evelyn Brooks**, calls **Dirksen Room 511** in January 2027.

---

## 1. Wednesday Afternoon, March 14, 2007 (`4:15 PM`): How Chris Scrambled the Dormitory Database

How did every dormitory room assignment in **Barton Hall** and **Cantor Hall** end up scrambled on Wednesday evening?

1. **An Unattended Housing Terminal on `Quantum OS 2000 Professional`:**
   At `4:15 PM` on Wednesday, March 14, 2007, a housing clerk in the **Bates-Harding Building** stepped away from her desk for ten minutes without locking her workstation, leaving the campus residential database application open under a local `Administrator` session.
2. **Swapping the Room Keys & Locking Out the IT Staff:**
   **Christopher Vance (`Chris`)**—who was furious at Katie and Nate after being humiliated in the therapeutic pool the afternoon before, and who had already targeted twenty-one-year-old **Natalie Brooks**—slipped into the housing office, ran an bulk update query that randomized dozens of male and female room assignments across Barton Hall (`deliberately assigning himself a keycard and printout slot for Natalie's room on the women's wing while routing himself past Katie's room`), printed the manipulated `5:00 PM` evening roster to the Barton Hall front-desk laser printer, and **changed the database administrator password** so the evening residential staff could not log into the server to verify or revert the table.
3. **Blind Bureaucratic Compliance at the Barton Hall Desk:**
   When the `6:00 PM` shift change arrived at Barton Hall and the computer terminal refused the evening supervisor's password, the residential staff—trained never to question a printed Bates-Harding directive—blindly enforced the paper printout, handing out reassigned magnetic keycards across both wings despite students protesting that men were being placed on the women's corridor and women on the men's corridor.

---

## 2. Thursday Morning, March 15, 2007 (`6:30 AM – 10:00 AM`): The Cover-Up & Why Nate and Katie's `Level 1` Meeting Was Canceled

While Nate and Katie were waiting in **Mr. Alderman's** Web Applications Developer classroom on Thursday morning expecting to be summoned at `10:00 AM` by their vocational counselor and slapped with a punitive **`Level 1` Restriction & Behavioral Contract** over Tuesday night's Rec Hall seasonal closet write-up, the second floor of the **Bates-Harding Building** was in full crisis-containment mode:

* **`6:45 AM` — Discovering What Chris Did to Natalie:**
   When morning dorm aides found a bleeding, traumatized **Natalie Brooks** crying in her room—understanding that what Chris had done to her was physically painful, even though her intellectual disability prevented her from comprehending the nature or long-term consequences of the sexual assault—the dorm supervisor notified the RRC Director's office instead of dialing `911` or the **Virginia State Police**.
* **`7:50 AM` — Putting Chris on a Bus in Staunton Without Calling Police:**
   Terrified that a felony rape investigation on campus—coming less than forty-eight hours after the same male client had broken Katie Prairie's nose in the therapeutic pool—would trigger an immediate state inspection, negative newspaper coverage, and a freeze on new client referrals (`"butts in seats"`), RRC administration quietly packed Christopher Vance's duffel bag, drove him in an unmarked Center van to the Greyhound bus station in **Staunton** at `7:50 AM`, and put him on a bus out of Augusta County without ever notifying law enforcement.
* **`8:30 AM` — Bleaching the Sheets, Holding Natalie in the Infirmary, & Falsifying `"Homesickness"` (`Status 28`):**
   Housekeeping was ordered to strip Natalie's bed and wash the bloodied sheets in industrial bleach in the campus laundry. When Natalie's mother and legal guardian, **Evelyn Brooks**, called to check on her daughter, RRC staff lied to her over the telephone—claiming Natalie was merely having a mild *"homesickness episode"*—and kept Natalie isolated inside the campus infirmary until Mrs. Brooks drove up on Friday, March 16, discovered her daughter's injuries at an Interstate 64 rest stop, and rushed her to the hospital emergency room for a forensic SANE exam. In DARS's mainframe in Richmond, RRC coded Natalie's departure as a voluntary *"homesickness"* withdrawal under **`Status 28` (*"Unsuccessful Rehabilitation — Client Dropped Out"*)**—the exact same `Status 28` code placed on Katie and Nathaniel Prairie's files when they left with **Tina** that Friday afternoon.
* **`10:00 AM` — Why Nate and Katie Were Never Called Into the Counselor's Office:**
   With the IT department spending all day Thursday rebuilding the corrupted dormitory database from tape backups and the administration frantically covering its tracks over Chris and Natalie, **nobody in Bates-Harding had the time or the stomach to haul Nate and Katie into an office at `10:00 AM` over Tuesday night's seasonal closet write-up**—buying the twins two uninterrupted days (`Thursday and Friday, March 15–16`) in Mr. Alderman's lab to copy the entire **`PHP 5`** and **`SQL`** curriculum onto their personal laptops before rolling out of Fishersville forever.

title: The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Closet Door Got Them Caught
subtitle: What Happened Across the Courtyard in Barton Hall & The Hookup Closet Irony Neither Twin Ever Knew
location: Barton Hall & Campus Recreation Hall, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center, Fishersville, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 6, Chapter 2, Part 2)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 6, Chapter 2, Part 2: Caught Sleeping Together in a Closet
summary: Behind-the-scenes breakdown of how Barton Hall staff knew to search the Rec Hall after the 11:00 PM Level 2 bed check—and why locking the normally unlocked door of a notorious student hookup closet is what actually got Nate and Katie caught.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie), the narrative camera is locked strictly to **Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view**. Once Nate and Katie slip down the darkened rear corridor of the **Rec Hall** at `10:44 PM` on Tuesday, March 13, 2007 and lock themselves inside the dark seasonal storage closet, they cannot see what is happening across the courtyard in **Barton Hall** at `11:00 PM`—and neither Nate, Katie, nor the main-novel text ever knows that **locking the closet door from the inside** is the exact thing that got them caught. This Backstage bonus feature reveals what happened on the other side of that solid-wood closet door.

---

## 1. The `11:00 PM` Level 2 Curfew Bed Check in Barton Hall & How Staff Knew to Search the Rec Hall

Across the courtyard in **Barton Hall**, the eleven-o'clock **Level 2** curfew bed check arrived right on schedule at `11:00 PM`.

* **On-Campus vs. Off-Campus Movement Rules (`Levels 2, 3, & 4`):**
  At **Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center (`RRC`)**, clients who were not under a punitive **`Level 1`** disciplinary restriction—which included **`Level 2`** clients in Barton Hall—did **not** have to sign in or sign out when traveling between buildings or points *on* the RRC campus (such as rolling from Barton Hall to the cafeteria, the Bates-Harding classrooms, or the Rec Hall). Passes and sign-outs applied **only when a client was leaving the RRC campus**:
  * **`Level 2` (`Barton Hall`):** Required a signed yellow paper **`Pass`** to leave campus independently—or Level 2 clients could sign up at the **Rec Hall desk** for a **Center-sponsored trip** to places like **The Spot** or **ValueMart** (which counted as getting a Pass, since the trip roster documented why they were off campus).
  * **`Level 3` (`Cantor Hall`):** Only needed to **sign out** in the dorm ledger when leaving the RRC campus (no paper pass required).
  * **`Level 4` (`Cantor Hall`):** Could simply **come and go off campus as they pleased** (no pass and no sign-out required).
* **Connecting the Dots Between Barton Hall and the Rec Hall (`11:00 PM – 11:15 PM`):**
  Because no sign-out was required for moving between buildings on campus, there was no paper trail at the Barton Hall front desk showing where Nate and Katie had gone after supper. When the dorm aides walked the `11:00 PM` bed-check rounds and discovered that **neither** Nathaniel Prairie on the men's wing **nor** Katie Prairie in `Room 157` on the women's wing was in bed—and verified at the front desk that neither twin had an off-campus Pass or Center trip sign-up on file—they knew both twins were still somewhere on campus.
* Dorm staff immediately called over to the **Rec Hall** right as the building was locking up after its `11:00 PM` closing time for Level 3 and Level 4 clients. The evening Rec Hall staffer immediately remembered seeing the twenty-one-year-old twins sitting together in their corner booth all night long—and realized that after seeing them roll toward the restrooms right before the `10:45 PM` Level 2 departure call, **he had never seen their two wheelchairs roll out the front glass doors toward Barton Hall!**

---

## 2. Why Locking the Door Is What Actually Got Nate and Katie Caught (`The Hookup Closet Irony`)

What Nate and Katie had no way of knowing when they slipped down the darkened rear corridor of the Rec Hall at `10:44 PM` was the secret campus reputation of that walk-in seasonal storage closet:

1. **A Known Campus Hookup Spot With a Normally Unlocked Door:**
   Because RRC's strict rule against clients having sex applied **at any time of day or night** anywhere on campus (and carried automatic expulsion for both clients), couples constantly looked for blind spots away from the dorm aides. That walk-in seasonal storage closet at the end of the darkened rear Rec Hall corridor was a **well-known spot where clients sneaked off to have sex**—and its brass doorknob was **normally left unlocked** by maintenance.
2. **What Would Have Happened If Nate and Katie Had Left the Door Unlocked:**
   When the night supervisor and the Rec Hall staffer walked down the rear corridor at `11:25 PM` sweeping the building, the staffer reached out and tried the brass doorknob of the seasonal storage closet as a routine check.
   * **Had Nate and Katie NOT twisted the interior thumb-turn lock:** The staffer would have turned the doorknob, felt that the door opened smoothly like normal, assumed nobody was locked inside, **never spotted Nate and Katie** tucked quietly in the pitch dark on the floor behind the parked wheelchairs and lumpy canvas bags of winter coats and stage curtains, and **moved right on to search the next building on campus for the twins!**
3. **The Dead Giveaway (`*Rattle, Rattle*`):**
   Instead, the instant the night supervisor grabbed the brass knob and felt that a **normally unlocked storage closet door was locked from the inside**, he knew with 100% certainty that two clients had locked themselves inside that closet. That is why he didn't knock or ask if anyone was in there—he immediately pulled out his master key ring, unlocked the cylinder, flung the door wide open with his flashlight aimed at the floor, and barked:
   > *"Aha! I knew it! What the hell do you two think you're doing locking yourselves inside a dark closet to have sex?!"*
4. **Why Nate and Katie Never Realized the Irony:**
   From Nate's and Katie's perspective inside the dark closet, they had already heard plenty of stories from other students during their first week and a half about clients sneaking off to have sex being a rampant thing at RRC. The second the night supervisor unlocked the door and shouted *"Aha! I knew it!"*, Nate and Katie simply figured in hindsight that this back closet was probably one of the places where clients got caught hooking up—never realizing for the rest of their lives that **locking the door from the inside** is the only reason they were found that night!

---

## 3. Why the Night Supervisor Froze at `11:25 PM` When They Dared Him to Call Their Father

When the night supervisor threatened to kick them out of the Center and Nate and Katie called his bluff at `11:25 PM`—daring him to walk right down the corridor to the **Rec Hall's front-desk telephone** and wake up their father **David Prairie** in Alexandria right then and there to come pick them up—two institutional realities collided in the supervisor's head:

* **RRC's Internal `"Butts in Seats"` Headcount Quota:**
  While Nate and Katie only suspected it at the time (a suspicion Katie later confirmed and weaponized as a Virginia legislator and United States Senator in **Dirksen Room 511**), RRC's operational budget and quarterly utilization metrics in Richmond depended heavily on keeping dormitory beds and classroom seats occupied (`"butts in seats"`). Expelling two high-aptitude Web Applications Developer students at `11:25 PM` on a Tuesday night—five hours after the female twin's nose had been broken open in the therapeutic pool by a male classmate—meant explaining two sudden mid-week vacancies and an unreportable natatorium injury to the Director and to a furious father driving down Interstate 81 from Northern Virginia.
* **Punting to Thursday Morning's `Level 1` Restriction Meeting:**
  Knowing that Nate and Katie's regular vocational counselor was off work on Wednesday (`March 14`), the night supervisor backed all the way down from his expulsion threat, logged the incident in the overnight residential blotter (*"the Chickenshit Report"*), and punted the problem to Thursday morning at `10:00 AM`—where staff intended to intimidate the twins with a **`Level 1` Restriction & Behavioral Contract** instead.

title: The Unopened RRC Staff Dossier: Form A vs. Form B & The Unsigned Level 1 Contract
subtitle: How Nate and Katie Presented on Paper to Fishersville Staff, the 1996 Exam Battery Trap, & The Punishment Contract Destroyed by Wednesday Night's Chaos
location: Testing Table Two & Bates-Harding Administration Building, Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center, Fishersville, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 6, Chapters 1–3)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 6, Chapter 1, Part 2: Rushing Voc Eval in One Week
summary: Inside the internal RRC staff notes on 'Prairie, Nathaniel' and 'Prairie, Katie'—why Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller handed them alternating Form A and Form B test booklets expecting them to cheat, why VITA locked down the lab on Quantum OS 2000 Professional, and the drafted Level 1 Restriction Contract sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 6***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/twelve-days-at-roosevelt-rehabilitation-center-walking-out-for-good/barton-hall-check-in-rushing-voc-eval-in-one-week-door-greeter/part-1-sunday-check-in-at-barton-hall-the-opposite-gender-dorm-rule-expelling-the-creepy-roommate), readers experience the twelve days at **Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center (`RRC`)** (`March 4–16, 2007`) through twenty-one-year-old **Nathaniel Prairie's** eyes. This Backstage dossier opens the internal Bates-Harding staff folder to show how the twins looked on paper to RRC evaluators and dorm supervisors—and reveals the drafted **`Level 1` Restriction & Mandatory Separation Contract** sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning, March 15, 2007 that the twins never even saw before walking out of Fishersville forever.

---

## 1. How Nate and Katie Presented on Paper to RRC Staff by Day 10 (`"Two Unusually Aggressive, Rule-Lawyering Siblings"`)

To readers who have followed Katie and Nate from childhood, their fierce boundaries at RRC are 100% earned self-protection. To RRC's institutional bureaucracy in Fishersville, however, the twenty-one-year-old twins from Virginia Beach looked like an unprecedented administrative headache from the hour they rolled through the doors of **Barton Hall** on Sunday afternoon, March 4, 2007:

1. **Sunday Afternoon (`March 4 — Day 1`):**
   Within twenty minutes of check-in, both twins loudly confronted a residential aide for grabbing their wheelchair push-handles without consent, demanded that an opposite-gender twin brother and sister be allowed to share a single dormitory room, and—before midnight—got Katie's first assigned `Room 157` roommate expelled from the Center for bringing alcohol into the dorm and sexually harassing Nate.
2. **Wednesday Afternoon (`March 7 — Day 4`):**
   Instead of docilely spending two to three weeks putting metal pegs into wooden holes in **Vocational Evaluation (`Voc Eval`)** so RRC could bill DARS for fifteen days of evaluation units, the twins publicly backed **Ms. Hollis** and **Mr. Miller** into a corner in front of all four break tables—threatening to call their father **David Prairie** in Alexandria and pack their bags that night unless the entire two-day **Web Applications Developer** technical exam battery was placed on `Testing Table Two` at `8:30 AM` sharp on Thursday morning.
3. **Thursday Afternoon (`March 8 — Day 5`):**
   When their Vocational Evaluator tried to steer Katie toward a **Waynesboro ValueMart door-greeter partnership** and urged both twins to *"practice independence by separating from each other during the day,"* they flatly rejected both recommendations—choosing to stay stuck indefinitely on **`Level 2` in Barton Hall** (`requiring a signed yellow paper Pass just to leave campus`) rather than stop holding hands or stop sitting together.

---

## 2. Thursday Morning, March 8, 2007 (`8:30 AM – 11:45 AM`): Why `Form A` and `Form B` Backfired on Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller

When **Ms. Hollis** and **Mr. Miller** laid the two thick manila exam packets onto **Testing Table Two** at `8:30 AM` on Thursday, March 8, both evaluators were smugly convinced they had set a trap the twins could not beat:

* **Expecting the Twins to Cheat Off Each Other:**
  Because Nate and Katie refused to sit at separate tables, Mr. Miller deliberately placed **`Form A`** (`pale blue cover sheet`) in front of Nate and **`Form B`** (`canary yellow cover sheet`) in front of Katie, with the multiple-choice questions scrambled in different orders—and then paced three feet behind their wheelchair push-handles for three hours straight waiting to catch them whispering or peeking at each other's bubble sheets.
* **Why Neither Twin Needed to Glance Sideways Once:**
  What Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller failed to grasp was that Nate and Katie had just graduated with **Associate of Applied Science degrees in Information Systems Technology (`3.9+ GPA`)** from the **Community College of Hampton Roads (`CCHR`)** twelve weeks earlier. When the twins opened the laminated 1996-vintage RRC test booklets—filled with `HTML 3.2` `<font>` and `<blink>` tags, `Netscape Navigator 3.0` frameset questions, `14.4 kbps` dial-up modem baud rates, and `Windows 95` `AUTOEXEC.BAT` prompts—both twins were internally disgusted that the Commonwealth of Virginia was using an eleven-year-old exam battery to gatekeep a 2007 web-development program.
* **The `11:45 AM` Score Sheet Shock:**
  Without exchanging a single word or look for three hours and fifteen minutes, Nate scored **`99.2%` on `Form A`** and Katie scored **`99.6%` on `Form B`**—forcing a tight-lipped Ms. Hollis to sign their one-week Vocational Evaluation completion forms before lunch.

---

## 3. Why the Bates-Harding Computer Lab Was Locked Down on `Quantum OS 2000 Professional`

When Nate and Katie rolled into **Mr. Alderman's** Web Applications Developer classroom on Monday morning, March 12 (`Day 8`), they were stunned to discover that RRC's computers were running seven-year-old **`Quantum OS 2000 Professional`** locked down so tightly by the **Virginia Information Technologies Agency (`VITA`)** that students in a web-development program didn't even have local administrator permissions to start an `Apache` web server or a local `SQL` database service.

Behind the scenes, Mr. Alderman had spent two years begging VITA's regional helpdesk in Richmond to grant local sandbox permissions for his classroom towers. VITA had refused every ticket—classifying student vocational lab machines under the exact same statewide lockdown policy as public-facing DMV lobby kiosks, and forcing Mr. Alderman to teach server-side **`PHP 5`** and **`SQL`** out of photocopied paper binders.

---

## 4. The Drafted Thursday Morning `Level 1` Contract Nate and Katie Never Had to Refuse (`March 15, 2007, 10:00 AM`)

After the night supervisor caught Nate and Katie locked inside the Rec Hall seasonal storage closet at `11:25 PM` on Tuesday, March 13 and wrote them up in the overnight residential blotter (*"the Chickenshit Report"*), their vocational counselor returned to work on Thursday morning, March 15 and printed a two-page **`Level 1 Disciplinary Restriction & Mandatory Sibling Separation Contract`** for their scheduled `10:00 AM` meeting:

* **Clause 1 (`Level 1 Campus Restriction`):** Revoking all off-campus pass privileges for 30 days and requiring 30-minute sign-in checks at the Barton Hall desk every evening.
* **Clause 2 (`Mandatory Daytime & Evening Separation`):** Prohibiting `Prairie, Nathaniel` and `Prairie, Katie` from sitting at the same cafeteria table, occupying the same Rec Hall booth, or having physical contact (`including holding hands`) anywhere on the RRC campus.

Had their counselor called them into his office at `10:00 AM` and slid that contract across his desk, Nate and Katie would have laughed in his face, called **David Prairie** from the counselor's own desk phone, and left RRC on Thursday afternoon instead of Friday. Instead, because **Christopher Vance's** Wednesday-night dorm-database hack and Thursday-morning cover-up threw the entire Bates-Harding administration into full panic mode, that unsigned `Level 1` contract sat forgotten in their counselor's inbox—until **U.S. Senator Katie Prairie's** investigators subpoenaed the unredacted 2007 file twenty years later.

title: The Sunward Tropics Security File & How Brenda Lost the 'Prairie' Surname
subtitle: Inside Attorney Arthur Vance's Settlement Trap, the $6,400 Cruise Credit-Card Debt, & The Va. Code § 20-121.4 Maiden Name Restoration Order
location: Law Offices of Arthur Vance, Independence Boulevard & Virginia Beach Circuit Court, Virginia Beach, Virginia
recipient: Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 3, Chapter 2, Part 5 & Chapter 3, Part 1)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 3, Chapter 3, Part 1: The Fault-Grounds Filing & The Protective Order
summary: What happened behind closed doors when Brenda's attorney walked into Arthur Vance's conference room to view the M/S Sunward Tropics Deck 4 security tape—and how Katie and Nate's request cost Brenda the Prairie family name.
markdown:
> **Archival Note:** In [***Katie & Nathaniel — Episode 3, Chapter 3, Part 1***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/katie/sixteen-summer-sanctuary/junior-year-at-northwood-high-the-prognosis/part-1-the-fault-grounds-filing-the-protective-order-junior-year-at-northwood-high-school), sixteen-year-old **Katie** and **Nathaniel Prairie** sit with their father **David Prairie** in family law attorney **Arthur Vance's** office on Monday, August 27, 2001 and ask whether the divorce decree can force their mother to surrender the surname **`Prairie`** and revert to her maiden name, **`Walsh`**. Because neither twin ever had to sit across a table from Brenda again, they only heard the result from their father after the decree was entered. This Backstage dossier reveals what happened inside Arthur Vance's conference room when Brenda and her counsel tried to contest the divorce.

---

## 1. The *M/S Sunward Tropics* Evidentiary Packet (`August 22–26, 2001`)

When the **Staff Captain** and **Chief Security Officer** of the ***M/S Sunward Tropics*** handed **David Prairie** a sealed manila envelope at the Port Canaveral gangway on Sunday morning, August 26, 2001, *Sunward Cruise Lines* was protecting itself against potential maritime premises-liability litigation by documenting beyond all dispute why a passenger had been confined to her stateroom and permanently banned from the fleet. Inside the envelope were four notarized records:

1. **Duplicate VHS Security Tape (`CAM-04B — Deck 4 Forward Stairwell Landing, Aug 22, 2001, 15:31:40–15:34:12`):**
   Time-stamped surveillance video showing sixteen-year-old Nathaniel and Katie sitting exhausted on the padded alcove bench holding hands after climbing four decks of stairs with progressive neuromuscular weakness, Brenda screaming inches from their faces over the *"Captain Barnaby's Pirate Parade"* children's character meet-and-greet, Brenda raising her right arm to strike Nathaniel across the face, and David stepping squarely between his wife and his children to block the blow before two uniformed shipboard security officers intervened.
2. **Shipboard Breathalyzer & Medical Brig Log (`15:48 EDT`):**
   Documenting Brenda's blood-alcohol concentration (`0.16% BAC`) at three-forty-eight in the afternoon and her verbal threats against the ship's purser and security staff.
3. **Captain's Master Log Extract & Stateroom 6004 Reassignment Order:**
   Documenting the Captain's order moving David, Nathaniel, and Katie to an accessible midship stateroom (`Stateroom 6004`) with two loaner manual wheelchairs while confining Brenda to the original interior cabin for the remainder of the Nassau voyage.
4. **Permanent Fleetwide Exclusion Notice:**
   Permanently barring Brenda from boarding any vessel operated by *Sunward Cruise Lines* or its corporate affiliates.

---

## 2. The Fourteen-Minute Settlement Conference (`Friday, October 19, 2001`)

When Brenda was served with the Virginia Beach Circuit Court fault-based **Complaint for Divorce** (`Va. Code § 20-91(A)(6)`, cruelty and reasonable apprehension of bodily hurt) and the **Family Abuse Protective Order** barring her from the marital home and from **Northwood High School**, she initially told her retained attorney that David was *"exaggerating a minor family disagreement on vacation"* and demanded spousal support and possession of the house.

On Friday afternoon, October 19, 2001, Brenda and her attorney walked into **Arthur Vance's** conference room off Independence Boulevard for a discovery preview. Mr. Vance did not argue. He simply pressed `PLAY` on the office VCR.

* **Minute 1 to Minute 3:** Brenda's attorney watched the `CAM-04B` tape in silence, read the Staff Captain's notarized brig report, and looked at Dr. Evelyn Carter's preliminary neuromuscular evaluation confirming that the sixteen-year-old twins Brenda had forced up four flights of shipboard stairs were losing functional motor strength in all four limbs.
* **Minute 4:** Brenda's attorney asked Mr. Vance to step out of the room for five minutes so he could speak with his client alone. Behind the closed door, her own lawyer told her bluntly that if a Virginia Beach Circuit Court judge watched that tape at a contested hearing, she would lose custody 100-to-0, be permanently barred from alimony under Virginia's fault statute, and be ordered to reimburse David for half of the **`$6,418.72`** she had secretly charged to the marital credit card to book the non-refundable Bahamas cruise—plus David's **`$4,500`** in legal fees.

---

## 3. The `Va. Code § 20-121.4` Maiden Name Stipulation

When Mr. Vance returned to the conference room, Brenda's attorney asked if David would consider a walk-away property settlement waiving reimbursement for the `$6,418.72` cruise debt and providing a modest one-time relocation check so Brenda could sign a lease on an apartment near Military Highway.

Mr. Vance slid two typed pages across the mahogany table:

1. **The Property & Custody Stipulation (`Va. Code § 20-109.1`):**
   Granting **David Prairie** permanent sole legal and physical custody of **Nathaniel** and **Katie Prairie**, permanent waiver of all spousal support, and a full release of Brenda's liability for the `$6,418.72` credit-card debt plus a `$3,000` relocation check—**strictly conditioned** upon Brenda's simultaneous execution of Document #2.
2. **The Joint Stipulation & Petition for Restoration of Former Name (`Va. Code § 20-121.4`):**
   Requiring Brenda to petition the Court as a mandatory, non-severable term of the Final Decree of Divorce to restore her maiden surname—**`Brenda Walsh`**—and requiring her to surrender her **`Prairie`** Virginia driver's license and Social Security card within thirty days of entry of the decree.

When Brenda protested that *"a husband can't make his ex-wife give back her married name,"* Mr. Vance looked across his glasses and delivered the message Katie and Nate had asked for:

> *"Your husband didn't ask for that clause, Ms. Walsh. Your sixteen-year-old son and daughter asked for it—and your husband told me he will happily take this tape to trial next Tuesday and let the judge saddle you with eight thousand dollars in debt and attorney's fees unless their wishes are respected in black and white."*

Brenda signed the **`Va. Code § 20-121.4`** stipulation in blue ink less than ninety seconds later. From that afternoon forward—through their Glenrock Mall near-miss in 2007 and their walk past **Suite 756 at Timberline Shopping Center** in 2027—she was legally **`Brenda Walsh`**, and never **`Brenda Prairie`** again.

Why did **David Prairie** remain so close to **Karen and Steve Fletcher** for the rest of his life—even though Karen was Brenda's younger sister and David's divorce settlement had just required Brenda to surrender her married surname?

   Karen hadn't been blindsided by the divorce. When Brenda blew `0.16% BAC` in the afternoon and raised her hand to sixteen-year-old Nate while both twins' legs were failing, Brenda crossed a hard safety line that neither Karen nor Steve could ever excuse.
2. **Brenda Burned the Earlton Court Bridge Herself (`Friday, October 19, 2001, 4:15 PM`):**
   Thirty minutes after leaving Arthur Vance's office with her `$3,000` relocation check, a furious Brenda drove straight to Karen and Steve's brick ranch on **Earlton Court**, expecting her younger sister to side with blood and cut off David over the divorce and the maiden-name clause. Instead, Karen looked her sister in the eye on the front porch and told her the plain truth: `Walsh` was Karen's own birth name too, Katie and Nate had asked for the name change only because they were afraid of Brenda using a `"Brenda Prairie"` ID at their school or doctors' offices, and David—a working single dad taking night classes at CCHR while raising two teenagers in brand-new electric wheelchairs—had *still* wiped out `$6,418.72` of Brenda's secret credit-card debt and handed her `$3,000` so she wouldn't end up on the street. When Karen refused to boycott David and offered to drive Brenda straight to an **Alcoholics Anonymous** meeting that evening instead, Brenda exploded—screaming that Karen was a *"traitor choosing an ex-in-law over your own flesh and blood"*—and stormed off the Earlton Court porch, cutting off **both** households for the next twenty-six years.
3. **David's Unspoken Rule Around Karen:**
   Just as importantly, after years of **David** and his retired mother **Ruth Prairie (`Grandma Ruth`)** watching young Brittany after school in Kempsville whenever `Pungo Ferry Road` flooded, David treated Karen's heartbreak with quiet class. Under David's roof on **Arvin Road**, he kept one lifelong unspoken rule: he never gloated about the divorce settlement or trash-talked Brenda in front of Karen, remembering that Brenda was still Karen's sister and that Karen was grieving the sister she used to have. That mutual decency—and their shared terror of what alcohol does to a family—is also why Karen and Steve stood squarely beside David on New Year's Day 2003 when seventeen-year-old Brittany brought gas-station alcohol into the Arvin Road living room.

title: Vectron Energy Corp.: 'Question The Rules' (1997–2001)
subtitle: From Deregulated Energy Trading Commercials to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act
location: Houston, Texas / Blacksburg, Virginia
relatedBookLabel: Episode 6, Chapter 2, Scene 1: Question The Rules: The Birth of Fin#
summary: In-universe corporate history of Vectron Energy Corp.'s 1997-2001 'Question The Rules' TV ad campaign, energy deregulation, and the birth of Z-SOX-302.
markdown:
Between **1997 and late 2001**, Americans turning on network television during Sunday afternoon football broadcasts or evening financial news could hardly go an hour without seeing the sleek, high-budget commercials of Houston-based **Vectron Energy Corp.**—each ending with the company's bold, silver-and-cobalt slogan:

> ***"Vectron. Question The Rules."***

---

## 1. The Public Pitch (`1997–2001`): Why "Question The Rules" Made Sense on TV

To the general public and Wall Street analysts in the late 1990s, *"Question The Rules"* was never perceived as a confession of financial fraud—it was celebrated as a manifesto for **market deregulation and technological disruption**.

For nearly a century prior to the mid-1990s, natural gas and electric utilities in the United States operated as sleepy, vertically integrated regional monopolies governed by rigid, decades-old rate tariffs. Vectron pitched itself to the public as the visionary technology company that dared to ask *why* energy had to be sold that way:

* **"Why Should Power Only Flow down One Wire?" (Wholesale Electricity & Natural Gas Deregulation):**
  Vectron's flagship 1998 television spot showed a gray, bureaucratic 1950s utility switchboard dissolving into a glowing fiber-optic trading floor, arguing that if families and factories could choose their long-distance phone carrier, they should be free to buy electricity and natural gas on an open, real-time spot market.
* **"Can You Trade the Weather? Question The Rules." (Weather Derivatives & Bandwidth Trading):**
  By 1999 and 2000, Vectron's ads showcased citrus farmers hedging against Florida freezes, municipal utilities locking in summer cooling costs through **VectronOnline** weather derivatives, and fiber-optic networks trading dark-fiber internet bandwidth like a commodity.

To millions of viewers—including **Daniel Brooks** watching the commercials in Christiansburg, Virginia—Vectron looked like the smartest company in America.

---

## 2. The December 2001 Collapse & The Birth of `Z-SOX-302`

Behind the glass facade in Houston, Vectron's executives were taking *"Question The Rules"* far beyond energy deregulation: they were questioning the fundamental rules of **Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)**.

Using mark-to-market accounting to book decades of speculative future energy profits on day one while hiding billions of dollars of toxic debt inside off-balance-sheet **Special Purpose Entities (`SPEs`)**, Vectron fabricated a mirage of endless growth—until the illusion imploded in **December 2001**, wiping out **\$70 billion in shareholder value**, evaporating **20,000 employee pensions**, and prompting the United States Congress to enact the **Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (SOX)**.

Fourteen years later, in **August 2015** ([*Episode 6, Chapter 1, Scene 4*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie/episode-6-fall-semester-2015/chapter-1-welcome-to-the-neighborhood/scene-4-question-the-rules-the-birth-of-fin)), CPI sophomore **Zoë Wren Brooks** studies the Vectron collapse in her **ACIS 3115** seminar alongside her **CS 3214 (*Compiler Design*)** coursework—inspiring her to create the **`Fin#`** functional financial programming language and her **`Z-SOX-302`** household audit engine, where every dollar is a conserved state and cooking the books is a compile-time error.

title: Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)
subtitle: Architectural, Geographic & Transit Dossier — Blacksburg, Virginia
location: Blacksburg, Montgomery County, Virginia
relatedBookLabel: The Eleventh Child: The Story of Jordan
summary: Complete in-universe campus guide to Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI), Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall, and the Poly Pass transit network.
markdown:
**Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)**—universally known across the New River Valley as **Poly** and home to the **CPI Forgers**—is a major public land-grant research university located on a high plateau in **Blacksburg, Montgomery County, Virginia**, nestled between the Blue Ridge and Allegheny mountains at an elevation of 2,080 feet.

Founded in **1872**, CPI serves as the central geographic anchor for both [***The Eleventh Child: The Story of Jordan***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie) (`2014–2016`) and the origin story of [**The Stardust Engine**](https://stardust.raggiesoft.com), whose five founding members—siblings **Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell** and their twin cousins **Evan and Tyler Wright**—formed their band in an unheated garage at the corner of Progress and Turner Streets while studying at CPI in **1986**.

---

## 1. Campus Identity, Colors & Architectural Signature

* **Athletic & Institutional Moniker:** **The CPI Forgers**
* **Official University Colors:** **Forger Maroon** (`#861F41`) and **Burnished Forge Gold / Burnt Orange** (`#E5751F`)
* **Architectural Stonework ("Appalachian Ironstone"):** Nearly every academic building and residence hall flanking the central campus is constructed from rough-hewn, ashlar-cut dolomitic limestone quarried locally in Montgomery County—giving the university its unmistakable Neo-Gothic fortress silhouette against the mountain sky.
* **Commonwealth Green:** The vast, oval central grass commons at the heart of campus, ringed by a one-way stone promenade and mature oak trees, connecting the northern academic terrace to the southern and western residential quads.

---

## 2. Key Campus Buildings & Landmarks

### Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall (`BLDG-014`)
Located on the West Campus residential quad along **Washington Street SW**, **Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall** ("Bennett Hall") is a six-story Ironstone residence hall housing approximately 400 students across five residential floors (`Floors 2–6`), overseen by Residence Director **Kelsey Brennan, M.Ed.** (`Room 104`) and ten undergraduate Resident Advisors (one male RA and one female RA per residential floor).

* **Hillside Topography & Dual Grade-Level Access:**
  Because Bennett Hall is built directly into the natural slope of the Washington Street SW hillside:
  * **Floor 1 (Lower Level / Inner Quad Level):** Opens at flat grade onto the lower brick pathways of the West Campus inner quad.
  * **Floor 2 (Washington Street SW Grade Level):** Opens at flat, zero-step grade directly onto the **Washington Street SW** sidewalk and ADA drop-off circle at the top of the hill. This unique two-level topography is why the **Office of Educational Accessibility (OEA)** designates **Room 214** on Floor 2 as the building's primary ADA wheelchair-accessible suite—allowing a manual or power wheelchair user to exit directly onto Washington Street SW at the top of the hill without needing an elevator, or take the central elevator down to Floor 1 for flat access to the inner quad.
* **The First-Floor Masonry Firewall (`Room 104` vs. `Suite 110–120`):**
  The first floor of Bennett Hall is physically divided into two completely air-gapped halves by an unbroken, solid interior masonry firewall with zero connecting doors:
  * **Western Half (Bennett Hall Residential Lobby):** Contains the 24-hour student front desk, residential mail room, TV lounge, staff workroom (`Room 106`), and Residence Director Kelsey Brennan's office (`Room 104`).
  * **Eastern Half (`Suite 110–120` — Central Office of Housing and Residence Life):** Houses the university-wide Housing Assignments & Operations annex, directed by **Dr. Alan Mercer** and Associate Director **David Thorne**. Walk-in visitors and contractors entering Central Housing from the outer quad cannot pass through the firewall into the residential dormitory.
* **Floor 2 Layout (`Suite 214/216`, `Room 215`, `Room 201`, & `Room 212A`):**
  * **Suite 214/216:** A two-room connecting suite sharing a central Jack-and-Jill bathroom. **Room 214** (`Jordan Fuller`, `Aubrie Jean Kelly`, `Madison Elizabeth Scott`) is equipped with an exterior Poly Pass RFID reader, an interior square stainless-steel `PUSH TO OPEN` paddle wired to a **10-second residential motorized door opener**, a roll-under vanity sink, widened bathroom doorways with steel grab bars, and a lowered peephole. **Room 216** (`Zoë Wren Brooks`, `Lauren Nicole Barnes`, `Hannah Ashlee Parker`) adjoins via the shared suite bathroom.
  * **Room 215 (West Wing Female RA Single):** Positioned directly across the corridor from Room 214; occupied by Junior/Senior Nursing & Pre-OT major **Isabel Claire Dawson**.
  * **Room 201 (East Wing Male RA Single):** Positioned near the eastern stairwell; occupied by Junior Accounting major **Henry Walsh** (`2014–2015`) and Sophomore Engineering major **Garrett Reynolds** (`2015–2016`).
  * **Room 212A (Accessible Roll-In Shower Room):** Single-occupant, Poly Pass-encoded private ADA roll-in shower and dressing suite located thirty feet down the Floor 2 corridor from Room 214.

### Academic, Dining & Athletic Facilities
* **Callahan Hall:** Home to the **Office of Educational Accessibility (OEA)** (`Suite 210`), directed by **Patricia Higgins, M.S., CRC** (and Senior Director **Eleanor Higgins, M.Ed.**), where students receive classroom accommodations, assistive FM microphone kits, and ADA housing clearances.
* **Kepler Hall:** Home to the **Department of Physics & Astronomy**, featuring tiered lecture auditoriums with front-row wheelchair cutouts and rooftop observatory domes where **Dr. Alistair** teaches introductory and advanced Astrophysics.
* **Gable Hall:** Humanities and History building housing **Dr. Marcus Gable**'s Western Civilization and Roman History lecture halls.
* **Kincaid Commons:** The flagship multi-station West Campus dining hall steps from Bennett Hall.
* **The Foundry:** The official CPI campus bookstore and Forgers outfitter.
* **The Crucible:** CPI's 66,000-seat outdoor football stadium on the southern edge of campus, famous for shaking the entire Blacksburg valley when sixty-six thousand Forger fans jump in unison to the opening guitar riff of *"Enter the Crucible"*.

---

## 3. The Poly Pass & Regional Transit Ecosystem

Every matriculated CPI student is issued a **Poly Pass**—an encrypted smartcard University ID that serves simultaneously as a residence hall keycard, Kincaid Commons dining pass, library card, and **unlimited fare-free regional transit pass** across three interconnected public transit agencies:

1. **Blue Ridge Transit (BRT — Blacksburg & Christiansburg):**
   Operates the maroon-and-gold fleet of 40-foot and 60-foot articulated low-floor heavy-duty transit buses across the CPI campus loops (**Commonwealth Mall**, **West Campus Loop**, **Progress Street**) and down **U.S. Route 460 Business** (`Route 100`) to the **Pepper Plaza Transit Center** in **Christiansburg**.
2. **Radford Transit (City of Radford & Radford University):**
   Operates a fleet of 29-foot and 30-foot low-floor municipal buses pulsing every 30 minutes (`:15` and `:45`) at the **McConnell Transit Center** on the campus of **Radford University**, along with ***The Radford Connector*** linking Radford, the New River Valley Mall in Christiansburg, and CPI.
3. **Mountain Valley Transit (MVT — Roanoke Valley):**
   Connects the New River Valley regional commuter routes into downtown **Roanoke**, **Roanoke–Blacksburg Regional Airport (`ROA`)**, and **Star City General Hospital**.

  • Kepler Hall: Home to the Department of Physics & Astronomy, featuring tiered lecture auditoriums with front-row wheelchair cutouts and rooftop observatory domes where Dr. Alistair teaches introductory and advanced Astrophysics.
  • Gable Hall: Humanities and History building housing Dr. Marcus Gable's Western Civilization and Roman History lecture halls.
  • Kincaid Commons: The flagship multi-station West Campus dining hall steps from Bennett Hall.
  • The Foundry: The official CPI campus bookstore and Forgers outfitter.
  • The Crucible: CPI's 66,000-seat outdoor football stadium on the southern edge of campus, famous for shaking the entire Blacksburg valley when sixty-six thousand Forger fans jump in unison to the opening guitar riff of "Enter the Crucible".

3. The Poly Pass & Regional Transit Ecosystem

Every matriculated CPI student is issued a Poly Pass—an encrypted smartcard University ID that serves simultaneously as a residence hall keycard, Kincaid Commons dining pass, library card, and unlimited fare-free regional transit pass across three interconnected public transit agencies:

  1. Blue Ridge Transit (BRT — Blacksburg & Christiansburg):
    Operates the maroon-and-gold fleet of 40-foot and 60-foot articulated low-floor heavy-duty transit buses across the CPI campus loops (Commonwealth Mall, West Campus Loop, Progress Street) and down U.S. Route 460 Business (Route 100) to the Pepper Plaza Transit Center in Christiansburg.
  2. Radford Transit (City of Radford & Radford University):
    Operates a fleet of 29-foot and 30-foot low-floor municipal buses pulsing every 30 minutes (:15 and :45) at the McConnell Transit Center on the campus of Radford University, along with The Radford Connector linking Radford, the New River Valley Mall in Christiansburg, and CPI.
  3. Mountain Valley Transit (MVT — Roanoke Valley):
    Connects the New River Valley regional commuter routes into downtown Roanoke, Roanoke–Blacksburg Regional Airport (ROA), and Star City General Hospital.

title: The Stardust Engine: 1986 CPI Origins & 'Electric Color'
subtitle: From an Unheated Blacksburg Garage to the Cosmos
location: Corner of Progress & Turner Streets, Blacksburg, Virginia (CPI)
relatedBookLabel: Episode 6, Chapter 5, Scene 3: Electric Color
summary: How Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, Tyler, and Holly formed The Stardust Engine at CPI in 1986—and how their 1987 debut 'Electric Color' awoke Jordan in 2015.
markdown:
Before [**The Stardust Engine**](https://stardust.raggiesoft.com) became the flagship progressive synth-rock force of [**Engine Room Records**](https://engineroom.raggiesoft.com), they were five college students crammed into a drafty, unheated garage at the corner of **Progress and Turner Streets** in **Blacksburg, Virginia**, just off the campus of [**Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)**](/locations/cpi).

---

## 1. The True Meaning of "The Stardust Engine" (`1986`)

In the fall of **1986**, when twin cousins **Evan and Tyler Wright** transferred to CPI to join siblings **Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell**, the very first song the four musicians wrote together was an anthemic synth-and-guitar odyssey titled **[*"The Stardust Engine"*](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color?track=1-13-the-stardust-engine)**.

At first, the band was almost too nervous to shop that song around to record labels—because it was so deeply personal to who they were as CPI science and engineering students. The title celebrated their two greatest shared passions:
* **"Stardust":** Their awe for the cosmos, stellar nucleosynthesis, and deep-space astrophysics.
* **"Engine":** The rockets, propulsion systems, and human engineering built to take you there.

When they released their debut album [***Electric Color***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color) in the summer of **1987**, *"The Stardust Engine"* closed the record as Track 13.

### Why the Band Hated Apex Records' Corporate Nickname Gimmick
When **Apex Records** later signed the band, Apex's corporate marketing department tried to manufacture a cheap 1980s teen-idol branding gimmick—billing lead vocalist **Cassidy O'Connell** as *"Stardust"* and keyboardist/composer **Ryan O'Connell** as *"The Engine."*

Every member of the band **despised** that corporate branding gimmick, because reducing their band name to a pair of solo nicknames stripped away the actual meaning of the song: a five-person family united by their love of the cosmos (*Stardust*) and the rockets that carry humanity across the stars (*Engine*).

---

## 2. How *Electric Color* (`1987`) and *Starfield Calibration* (`1995`) Connect to *The Eleventh Child*

Twenty-eight years after *Electric Color* was pressed to vinyl in Blacksburg, its grooves spin once again in **Christiansburg, Virginia** on the Friday evening of **November 13, 2015** ([*Episode 6, Chapter 5: "An 80s Education"*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie/episode-6-fall-semester-2015/chapter-5-an-80s-education)):

1. **Awakening from a Grey World into *Electric Color*:**
   After **Mark Anderson** plays [*"An 80s Education"*](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-paper-wall/2003-eleventh-child-book-2?track=1-02-an-80s-education) in the living room of **412 Geneva Street**, **Daniel Brooks** pulls his original 1987 pressing of [***Electric Color***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color) from his walnut vinyl crate. When the needle drops onto Track 1 ([*"Electric Color"*](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color?track=1-01-electric-color)), something profound awakens inside nineteen-year-old Jordan—hearing a song born right at CPI that declares his world is no longer grey, *just color*.
2. **Astrophysics & *Starfield Calibration* (`1995`):**
   Later that same night ([*Scene 4: "Starfield Calibration"*](https://books.raggiesoft.com/aubrie/episode-6-fall-semester-2015/chapter-5-an-80s-education/scene-4-starfield-calibration)), Daniel pulls out The Stardust Engine's 1995 concept album [***Starfield Calibration***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/the-stardust-engine/1995-starfield-calibration)—a record inspired by deep-space optical navigation and how a spacecraft lost in the dark uses three fixed guide stars to triangulate its true position and plot its trajectory home. For Jordan and **Aubrie Jean Kelly**, both CPI Astrophysics majors who found their own guide stars in Suite 214/216, the album becomes the soundtrack of their lives.
